item.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
item.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. item.title: Kusal Mendis scripts history, joins Virat Kohli, Steve Smith and Joe Root in elite club
item.description: Kusal Mendis joined an elite group featuring Joe Root, Virat Kohli and Steve Smith after becoming the latest batter to score a century on his debut as a Test captain. The Sri Lankan made history against Pakistan on Wednesday, becoming the first player from his country to achieve the feat. Mendis, who took over as Sri Lanka's full-time Test captain from Dhananjaya de Silva last month, marked his leadership debut with a memorable unbeaten hundred. His knock also placed him among the prominent names in world cricket who have begun their Test captaincy careers with a century. The 31-year-old reached the landmark with a boundary off Razaullah in the third delivery of the 92nd over. Mendis also played a crucial role in Sri Lanka's recovery after the visitors found themselves struggling at 155/4 in 42 overs. He combined with his fifth-wicket partner to put together a massive 249-run stand. With the achievement, Mendis became the 37th cricketer overall to register a hundred in his first Test as captain. He is also only the second player after former England skipper Andrew Strauss to score a century on his Test captaincy debut against Pakistan. The list of players to have accomplished the feat includes some of the biggest names in the game. India's Virat Kohli scored 115 against Australia in Adelaide in 2014, while Steve Smith followed with 133 against India in Brisbane later that month. England's Joe Root also made a memorable start to his captaincy tenure, scoring 190 against South Africa at Lord's in 2017. Other notable names on the list include Sunil Gavaskar, Greg Chappell, Alastair Cook, Kevin Pietersen and Shubman Gill, who scored 147 against England at Leeds in 2025. South Africa's Wiaan Mulder also made history with an unbeaten 367 against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo in 2025. Mendis' century also brought another significant personal milestone. During his innings, he crossed 13,000 runs in international cricket, becoming only the eighth Sri Lankan batter to reach the mark across all three formats. Kumar Sangakkara remains Sri Lanka's leading run-scorer in international cricket with 27,757 runs from 587 matches between 2000 and 2015. Mahela Jayawardene occupies second place with 25,688 runs, followed by Sanath Jayasuriya with 20,966.

item.title: Cubs Reportedly Interested In Free Agent Brewers Champion
item.description: pitcher Dustin May The Chicago Cubs are in desperate need of starting pitching and are reportedly showing interest in Milwaukee Brewers free agent Dustin May. "Free agent RHP Dustin May is drawing interest from a broad group of teams that includes the Cubs," wrote MLB Network's Jon Morosi on Wednesday. May started the season with the St. Louis Cardinals and was traded to the Brewers at the trade deadline. Originally, the Brewers hoped he would be a key part of their rotation in the postseason, but after some good moments, May struggled to find consistency. Eventually, the Brewers ended up going with Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson and Robert Gasser as their postseason starters, and then decided to throw a bullpen day instead of a fourth starter. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! May did get opportunities as the starter or bulk pitcher on those days, but he was not a traditional starter. However, he helped them win the World Series, and then declined his option. The Cubs could see him as a bounce-back candidate, and he would not be too expensive. Right now, the Cubs are going into the season with Edward Cabrera and Justin Steele at the top of their rotation. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, Clay Holmes and Kevin Gausman are free agents, and Cade Horton and Ben Brown could miss most of the season. May is a veteran starter who had a lot of good moments last season. He has postseason experience and would be a solid option for the Cubs. Stealing him away from a rival would just be icing on the cake. More MLB: Brewers Ace Wins 2026 NL Cy Young Award Unanimously

item.title: Owono undecided over future following De Miguel death
item.description: Owono has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea but was not called up during the most recent international window [Getty Images] FC Andorra manager Carles Manso says goalkeeper Jesus Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. Owono was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during a Spanish second division match on 2 November, with the Tenerife forward passing away the following day in hospital. Manso said the goalkeeper, 25, is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return. "What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him," Manso said. "We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return. "When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so]." Andorra released a statement on behalf of Owono on 4 November, with the Equatorial Guinea keeper saying he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life". He added: "I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him." The team will return to action for the first time since De Miguel's death on Saturday when they face Almeria in the Spanish second division. item.title: Kyle Busch Posthumously Wins Most Popular Driver Award
item.description: Feb 11, 2026; Daytona Beach, Florida, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Kyle Busch (8) during qualifying for the Daytona 500 at Daytona International Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Kyle Busch finally won the Most Popular Driver Award after his death , securing a record 261,612 votes according to the National Motorsports Press Association. This total shattered previous marks and placed the driver ahead of Kyle Larson and third-place finisher Carson Hocevar. Fans cast these ballots to honor a man who spent 25 years in the national series as a figure many loved to boo. The award was presented at the season-ending ceremony in Miami on Tuesday, where his wife Samantha accepted the trophy on his behalf. Busch had spent decades chasing this specific honor while dominating the sport in every other way. He secured Cup championships in 2015 and 2019 and earned 63 victories at NASCAR’s top level. His career also included a record 234 wins across all three national series. Despite those numbers, the popularity trophy remained out of reach until 2026. Samantha Busch recalled how much the award meant to him before the ceremony even began. “Winning the Most Popular Driver, he wanted it so bad. He would try to rally the fans, and there was one year, I think, either he didn’t see Chase [Elliott] out here, or maybe Chase didn’t come, and he was like, ‘I got it. I got it,’ and he was so excited. And then he didn’t. And so he called NASCAR, and he was like, ‘I want to see the numbers. How far off was I? Was I close?’ Kyle was very competitive, and he took this no differently,” Samantha said before Tuesday’s ceremony, according to Fox Sports . She noted that he had once called NASCAR officials just to find out how close he had come to winning. A Shift in the Fan Vote The result marked a major shift from how fans viewed Busch during his life. For years, his aggressive driving and honest personality made him one of the most divisive stars in the sport . Spectators would pack the stands just to see what he would do next, often cheering when his rivals beat him. Yet he never changed his approach to please the crowd. While maintaining his true character, Samantha recalled that history during her acceptance speech. “Kyle never changed who he was to make people like him.” This win proved that popularity does not always require universal approval. Chase Elliott played a key role in making this outcome possible. Elliott had won the award for eight straight years from 2018 to 2025. He asked his fans to vote for Busch instead after withdrawing his name from the 2026 ballot. This move mirrored what Bill Elliott did in 2001 after Dale Earnhardt’s fatal crash. That year, Earnhardt earned his sole Most Popular Driver award, which was also his first. Following his death, Busch became only the second driver to secure the Cup award. The last time a driver won posthumously was when Earnhardt won, and before that, only drivers with the surnames Earnhardt or Elliott

item.title: Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million Gemini Space Station has sold its already shuttered U.K. and European operations to Singapore stablecoin payments firm KAST for less than $10 million, according to CoinDesk reporting , as the exchange prepares to report third-quarter results after Thursday’s close. Gemini declined to comment. A spokesperson for KAST would not discuss the transaction, but said the company is actively looking at acquisitions as its revenue and footprint grow. Neither firm has issued a public confirmation of a sale, and no regulator has announced a change-of-control approval. The disposal, if confirmed, would close a retreat Gemini laid out in February. On Feb. 4, the Nasdaq-listed company, known as Gemini (GEMI), approved a plan to exit and wind down its operations in the United Kingdom, the European Union and other European jurisdictions, and Australia, as part of a broader effort to cut expenses and support a path to profitability. It said it would keep operating in the United States and Singapore. The plan included a reduction in force of up to 200 employees in Europe, the United States and Singapore, or about 25% of Gemini’s global workforce as of that date. The company estimated about $11 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, mostly in cash, and said it expected the wind-down to be substantially completed in the first half of 2026. Reuters reported the job cuts the same day. Co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, who started Gemini in 2014 as a bitcoin exchange, told customers the firm would “double down on America” after foreign markets proved hard to win and stretched the company’s cost base. Gemini later told U.K., European Economic Area and Australian customers that their accounts would close on April 6, with withdrawals-only starting in early March. What would change hands in a sale is the leftover entities, staff and regulatory permissions from those already wound-down units, not Gemini’s core U.S. exchange. Buyers of shuttered crypto businesses often want the licenses more than the remaining operations. Any transfer of a licensed firm in the U.K. or the EU typically still requires a change-of-control review by local regulators before a new owner can run it. A payments firm with European ambitions KAST is a Singapore-based financial platform built on stablecoin rails. In March, it said it had raised $80 million in a Series A round co-led by QED Investors and Left Lane Capital. The company, founded in July 2024 by former Circle executive Raagulan Pathy, said it would use the capital for expansion, licensing and compliance. KAST provides dollar-denominated accounts, cross-border payments and cards that let consumers and businesses hold, move and spend stablecoins. In the March release, it said it had more than one million users and was processing nearly $5 billion in annualized transaction volume. Those figures have not been independently verified, and KAST

item.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
item.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely tipped to replace him. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United's statement said. "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club." United said they intended to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". - Chaos - Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. United, however, have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, most recently in charge of Germany, were touted as possible replacements but Pochettino has now emerged as the overwhelming favourite to succeed Carrick. The Argentine has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. - 'Legend' - But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new boss. item.title: UEFA fine Roma over fan clashes during Man United trip
item.description: UEFA fine Roma over fan clashes during Man United trip Roma have received a €20,000 fine from UEFA’s disciplinary body and a potential partial restriction on away ticket allocations for one of their upcoming European fixtures. UEFA sanctioned Roma after Giallorossi fans clashed with police following an away Champions League match against Manchester United on November 3. Roma fined after fans’ clashes at Man United ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 30: Fans of AS Roma show their support by displaying flags prior to the Serie A match between AS Roma and SSC Napoli at Stadio Olimpico on November 30, 2025 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Gazzetta reports that the Giallorossi have been fined €20,000 and received a second sanction that could affect one of their future away games in Europe. The European football governing body has ordered a partial restriction on away ticket allocations, reducing the number of tickets available to visiting supporters from 2.5% to 5%. This measure, however, has been suspended for two years and will only be activated if further clashes occur during the probationary period. MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Matheus Cunha of Manchester United scores his team’s third goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Bryan Cristante of AS Roma following defeat in the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Roma’s upcoming Champions League trip to Paris-Saint-Germain on November 25, however, is already being considered a high-risk fixture by local authorities. Among the matters of concern is the fact that PSG and Napoli ultras are twinned, not to mention that Roma ultras also clashed during their latest trip to France, where 13 of them were arrested for a Europa League game at Nice. The away allocation for PSG-Roma has already been reduced from 2,376 to 1,500 tickets, but, according to Gazzetta, if public security risks increase in the coming weeks, French authorities could even order the entire away end at the Parc des Princes to be closed.

item.title: Goalkeeper Martin returns to West Ham as coach
item.description: David Martin made more than 400 appearances during a 21-year senior career [Shutterstock] Former West Ham United goalkeeper David Martin has returned to the Championship club to head-up their academy and under-21s goalkeeper coaching department. The 40-year-old, who is the son of former Hammers defender Alvin Martin, has held previous coaching roles at Southend United, Ipswich Town and Chelsea from where he moves to the London Stadium. Martin made five Premier League appearances for West Ham, including keeping a clean sheet on his debut against Chelsea in November 2019. He started his career with AFC Wimbledon but is best known for a seven-year spell at MK Dons where he featured in more than 300 games in all competitions. item.title: Daniss Jenkins Explains What Has Clicked for the Pistons
item.description: The Detroit Pistons are off to a 7-3 start this season and visit the Washington Wizards again on Thursday night. When Detroit faced Washington on Monday, Daniss Jenkins earned a spot in the starting lineup next to Cade Cunningham for the first time this season. Jenkins sat down for a one-on-one video interview with WXYZ sports anchor Tina Nguyen . She asked him what has been impressive about the 7-3 start this season. Jenkins said , “I think the biggest thing was shooting. That was the biggest thing. The ability for us to come together so fast. We got new teammates, new guys coming in but we’re all just trying to get that identity back.” Nov 9, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Daniss Jenkins (24) is defended by Washington Wizards forward-center Anthony Davis (23) in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) What Daniss Jenkins Means by One Common Goal After winning 60 games last season, Detroit lost to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the second round of the NBA playoffs in Game 7. This season, the Pistons are looking for a different result in the playoffs. Even with new players on the team, they still have championship expectations. Jenkins said, “We all are working for one common goal to see how like you can come together and build that bond.” John Collins is one of the new players on the Pistons roster this season. He scored 24 points in the last game against the Wizards. Why Jenkins Earned a Spot in the Starting Five Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told the team’s website that Jenkins had earned more with the spark he gave Detroit off the bench, and that the staff had talked about improving the team’s starts. Jenkins lined up with Cunningham, Collins, Duncan Robinson and Ausar Thompson in the starting five on Monday and finished with 22 points, eight assists, six rebounds and four steals in 36 minutes of the 122-111 win. Jenkins Is Off to a Strong Start to the 2026-27 NBA Season Jenkins has played in 10 games this season for the Pistons. He is averaging 12.7 points per game, 3.6 rebounds per game, 4.7 assists per game, 0.1 blocks per game, and 0.8 steals per game. He should get another start against the Wizards on Thursday night. One of the most important things for Jenkins is that he is shooting 42.9% from three-point land, 45.2% from the field, and 91.7% from the free throw line. The 25-year-old is no doubt an important piece for this Pistons basketball team.

item.title: Braves Prospect Headlines AFL Fall Stars Game Roster
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The desert is ready for the 20th annual Fall Stars Game at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick, according to MLB.com . Top talents from the Arizona Fall League will square off in a contest fans can watch on MLB Network, the MLB app, or right here on the site. The game features a mix of the league’s best hitters and pitchers, including a standout Braves prospect who has drawn attention all season. The National League roster includes Tate Southisene, the shortstop for the Atlanta organization. Fans can follow the action with a live Gameday box score and check out scouting reports for every player on the field. The event also follows the Home Run Derby where Toronto’s Aaron Parker took the crown on Saturday night. The Week 5 Standouts Arizona Fall League action saw several players make their mark just before the All-Star weekend. Welbyn Francisca, a frequent name in these discussions, led the AFL in batting average at .419 and posted an OPS of 1.198. He also recorded 31 hits and 28 RBIs during the season. Other players stole the show with strong numbers. Zion Rose, the Kansas City outfielder, had six stolen bases and more RBIs than any other player during the week. Half of his hits went for extra-bases, boosting his slugging percentage. Antonio Anderson, a Boston infielder, slashed .455/.647/.727 with more walks than strikeouts. With 20 RBIs, he ranks fourth in the AFL and is one of nine players to post an OPS over 1.000. These stats show who is ready for the next level. Braves Prospects on Display Tate Southisene represents the Atlanta organization in a field packed with future stars. The shortstop is part of a deep group of young talent that includes Demetrio Crisantes and Aidan Miller. Crisantes is the top prospect for his team. Miller, a designated hitter for Philadelphia, leads the AFL in walks. The presence of these players shows the depth of the minor league system across the league. The pitching staff features key arms from both leagues. On the American League side, Patrick Reilly of Baltimore will take the mound. The matchup highlights the best young pitchers working toward the majors. Fans will see how these arms handle the pressure of a high-profile game. Tracking the Fall Stars The game offers a rare chance to see top prospects face each other in a competitive setting. Scouting reports are available for every player on the rosters. This allows fans to dig into the details of each hitter and pitcher before the first pitch. The event also is a look back at the week’s top performers and the history of the Fall Stars Game. It is a key stop on the road to the next season. Viewers can catch the live broadcast on MLB Network or stream it through the MLB app. The Gameday box score provides real-time updates for those following along digitally. item.title: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home”
item.description: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home” For someone who faithfully represented Brazil from the ages of 15 to 20, a two-year absence may have felt like an eternity. Between 2019 and 2024, Marlon Gomes played for Brazil’s Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-20 and Under-23 teams. With that kind of history, the path to the senior national team seems natural. Called up for the first time, the midfielder—matured by his journey “in his second home,” by overcoming the challenges of becoming a father at 15, and by the resilience needed to stay focused while playing in a country at war—now finds himself on the team he has always dreamed of playing for. “I spent a lot of time here, going back to the youth teams. I started coming to the national team at 15, so it has always been my second home. Whenever there was a call-up, I was there, along with Andrey. I have many friends I’ve known since the youth teams, and I’m very happy to see them again and to return (to the national team) after a long time, now with the senior team,” he said at a press conference on Thursday (12). Playing for Brazil, the Rio de Janeiro native won the South American Under-20 Championship and competed in the Under-20 World Cup and the CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament, as well as international friendly tournaments. Marlon Gomes at a press conference in Singapore during his first call-up to Brazil’s senior national team Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Experienced at youth international level, this time he is one of the newcomers among the 25 players selected by Carlo Ancelotti for the friendlies against Japan and Singapore. “I’m happy about this new project to bring fresh faces into the national team. I’m very happy, and my expectations about returning to the Brazilian national team couldn’t be higher. Now I’m fulfilling a dream with the senior team and being part of this new cycle. I have the highest hopes. This is my first time here. I hope to train well and learn as much as possible from the big-name players, and I hope I can play well so I can come back more often,” he said. A father at 15 A product of Vasco’s youth system, which he joined in 2017, Marlon Gomes became a father at a young age. His daughter Maitê was born when he was 15—a challenging age for someone who would have to balance fatherhood, the daily demands of football training and travel, and the dream of changing his family’s life. Despite the difficulties, he was determined to keep the promise he made to his mother and his daughter’s mother to grow personally and professionally. "I was very young and didn’t have the financial means. When my mother found out, we all cried together: me, her and my daughter’s mother. I promised to change our lives, and not just with empty words, but by becoming a great player and a respectable young man who would make it to the national team. I kept that promise," he stressed. item.title: Barcelona have zero intention of selling midfield star despite growing interest – report
item.description: Barcelona have zero intention of selling midfield star despite growing interest – report According to MARCA , Barcelona have no plans to part ways with fan-favourite midfielder Gavi despite his limited involvement under Hansi Flick this season. The 22-year-old La Masia graduate, for his part, is not entirely happy with his situation, but is also not considering leaving the club in the upcoming transfer window. Gavi going through a difficult phase It has been a difficult season so far for Gavi, who has lost his prominence in Flick’s setup at Barcelona. The Spanish midfielder has found minutes extremely hard to come by, owing to the immense competition for places. As things stand, the academy ace is behind Pedri, Rodri, Marc Bernal, Frenkie de Jong, Dani Olmo, and Fermin Lopez in the pecking order. It has led to him playing only a paltry 227 minutes across nine matches in all competitions this season. His lack of regular minutes even resulted in his omission from the Spain squad in the current international break. Gavi has seen his role reduce this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Given his situation, top clubs across Europe are starting to show an interest in the 2026 FIFA World Cup winner. Teams like Napoli and Bayern Munich have been credited with interest in Gavi, while several other major clubs have also asked about his situation. Gavi not for sale But, as far as Barcelona are concerned, the possibility of letting Gavi go in the upcoming January transfer window is completely off the table. Even though he has not played regularly, manager Flick continues to value the young midfielder and the qualities he offers. Gavi remains fully committed. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Meanwhile, Gavi himself has no desire to leave Barcelona amid the growing interest in his services. The 22-year-old Spaniard is understood to be unhappy with his playing situation, but also understands that the season is long and his opportunity will come. As such, he has continued to work hard despite his reduced role, maintaining his motivation and commitment to the group, which has impressed the coaching staff. The midfielder shares a special relationship with Flick, which has not been affected by his current situation either. For now, all parties remain on the same page, and there will no departure for Gavi come January.

item.title: Dortmund CEO Watzke asks Nmecha to refrain from religious celebration
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and SV Elversberg at Signal Iduna Park. (is associated with: «Dortmund CEO Watzke asks Nmecha to refrain from religious celebration») David Inderlied/dpa Borussia Dortmund CEO Hans-Joachim Watzke has asked midfielder Felix Nmecha to refrain from doing a controversial celebration in the future. “He was with the (Germany) national team and I was at home on the couch. We had a video call,” Watzke told the Ausgerechnet podcast. “If you realize that it’s dividing the fans, maybe then you’ll also have the insight to simply stop doing it. He wants to think about it.” Watzke emphasized that he didn't intend to prohibit religious gestures from devout Christians. "Nobody here wants to forbid anything, nobody wants to punish. We're relying more on understanding," he said. Nmecha's recurring goal celebration, in which he takes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling, has been heavily criticized, including by Dortmund's fan department. He explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength." The gesture is used by the network Ballers in God, which has been criticized for homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members. Ballers in God is a network of Christian footballers founded in 2015 that records and shares many such celebrations on social media. "When I look at what they stand for: Borussia Dortmund's core values and Ballers in God's basic principles aren't compatible," Watzke said. Nmecha has previously been criticized for religious content on social media, which has been deemed homophobic. He has rejected these accusations.

item.title: How FRANCE 24 traced Tehran-backed Afghan fighters from Syria to southeastern Iran
item.description: Members of the Tehran-backed Afghan Shia militia known as the Fatemiyoun division have resurfaced in Iran after largely disappearing from public view following the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government in Syria in 2024. FRANCE 24 used "martyrdom” announcements and the geolocation of videos shared on social media to trace their presence.

item.title: Ebonyi pensioners endorse Nwifuru for second term
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has endorsed Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election, citing his administration’s payment of outstanding pension and gratuity arrears dating back to 1996. The union also conferred an award on Nwifuru as the most pensioner-friendly governor in recognition of what it described as his commitment to the welfare of retired workers in the state. The endorsement was announced during the presentation of the award to the governor in Ebonyi State. The National President of NUP, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, represented by his deputy, Abdulahi Onuh, commended Nwifuru for clearing the backlog of pensions and gratuities owed to retired workers from 1996. Onuh described the achievement as significant, saying the governor had distinguished himself through his administration’s intervention in the welfare of pensioners. He said, “Clearing pensions and gratuity of pensioners from 1996 till date is not a small number of years. The Governor has written his name in gold. “While in Kano, I thought that the Governor of Kano State is number one. I never knew that coming to Ebonyi State, the Kano Governor will be number two. “To clear a backlog of pensions and gratuity from 1996 till date is a very big achievement. May God elongate the life of Ebonyi Governor. The Governor has done a lot.” He also commended the state government over plans to extend the state health insurance scheme to retirees, describing the initiative as another important intervention in their welfare. The NUP national leadership, however, urged the state government to implement pension increases and harmonisation of benefits, noting that pension increments were provided for under the Constitution. Onuh called on pensioners to reciprocate the governor’s gesture by voting for him in the 2027 election. He said, “You are indebted to the Governor. Use your PVCs and show him appreciation by voting for him in the 2027 general election. “When you go home, off your clothes and tell your children that as of two years back, they were taking you to the hospital every week. You were calling your children both home and abroad, bring me my medical allowance. “But the Governor has reduced the strength of your children in Nigeria and outside. Go and pay him back. Tell your children, tell your in-laws to pay the Governor back by voting for him.” Also speaking, the Ebonyi State Chairman of NUP, Comrade Anna Ibiam, said retired workers had endured years of unpaid pensions and gratuities before Nwifuru assumed office. She said some pensioners died while waiting for their entitlements, adding that the governor’s administration had changed the situation through regular pension payments and the clearance of outstanding gratuities. “Many of our colleagues died waiting without receiving their gratuity. May their souls rest in peace. “You came, Your Excellency, and you changed our story. You not only pay

item.title: At 44, England great James Anderson extends playing career with Surrey after shock Lancashire departure
item.description: At 44, James Anderson is not ready to walk away from cricket. England's legendary fast bowler is set to begin a new chapter in his illustrious career after joining Surrey for the 2027 county season, following the end of his 25-year association with Lancashire. Surrey confirmed the signing on Thursday, giving the veteran pacer an opportunity to continue playing at the highest level of county cricket. Anderson's move comes after Lancashire decided against renewing his contract for the upcoming season, bringing an unexpected end to his long association with his boyhood club. Despite the disappointment, Anderson has made it clear that he still has the hunger to compete, take wickets and contribute to a team's success. 'I still feel like I have a lot to offer': Anderson on Surrey move Anderson expressed his excitement about joining Surrey and said he was looking forward to contributing both on and off the field. "I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games," Anderson said in a statement. The former England international also highlighted his desire to help younger players develop their skills and progress towards representing the national team. "I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country," he added. According to British media reports, Anderson has signed an initial one-year deal with Surrey, with an option to extend his stay beyond the 2027 season. Lancashire exit ends 25-year association Anderson's move to Surrey follows a difficult few weeks after Lancashire opted not to renew his contract. The decision ended a 25-year relationship with the county where he began his professional career in 2001. The veteran pacer admitted he was shocked by the decision but remained determined to explore new opportunities rather than bring his playing career to an end. His departure came despite an impressive 2026 County Championship campaign, during which he claimed 50 wickets. Anderson had also captained Lancashire during the season, making the decision not to retain him a significant development. The fast bowler will now bring his experience and leadership to Surrey as he looks to make an impact in the 2027 campaign. Anderson's remarkable international career Widely regarded as one of the greatest fast bowlers in cricket history, Anderson retired from international cricket in 2024 after a career spanning more than two decades. He finished with 991 international wickets across formats, the highest tally by a fast bowler in men's international cricket. His Test record remains particularly remarkable, with 704 wickets in 188 matches, making him the most successful fast bowler in the history of the format. Anderson also claimed 269 ODI wickets and 18 T20I wickets for England. He made his international debut in 2002 and became the spearhead of England's pace attack across several generations.

item.title: 'Everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in' - Alan Shearer names Arsenal summer signing as the Premier League's early player of the season
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Alan Shearer has named Ezri Konsa as the Premier League's player of the season so far, insisting the Arsenal summer signing has been so good that nobody has even noticed William Saliba's absence. The England defender has been an ever-present for Mikel Arteta's league leaders, and Saliba's looming return from a back injury now leaves the Gunners with a big selection call. Shearer crowns Konsa early player of the season Alan Shearer believes Konsa has been the standout performer in the Premier League this season after a superb start to life at Arsenal. The 29-year-old completed a £55 million move from Aston Villa in the summer, ending a seven-year spell at Villa Park that brought a Europa League triumph. Speaking to Betfair, Shearer said: "I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa." Konsa has missed just one game so far, helping Arteta's side open up a five-point lead at the top of the table. Konsa makes Arsenal forget Saliba injury Arsenal signed Konsa partly to cover for Saliba, who returned from last summer's World Cup with a serious back injury. Instead, the England international has turned that absence into an afterthought for the reigning champions. Shearer added: "I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven't even really mentioned them missing William Saliba. The only time we've mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that's because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good." Ferdinand warns Arteta of a huge problem Rio Ferdinand recently made the same point on his YouTube channel: "Mikel Arteta has got a problem, he's got a huge problem now. What is he going to do when William Saliba is fit? Ezri Konsa has come into that back-four and he looks like he's been there for ten years." The former Manchester United defender added: "It's a problem but it's a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he's got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team. It's a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back." Arsenal head to Newcastle as Brighton give chase Arsenal return from the international break with a tricky trip to Newcastle at St James' Park, with Saliba closing in on a comeback. Brighton, who have won seven of their 10 league games, sit second. Shearer expects them to stay the course. "Brighton could be Arsenal's main challenge to the title this season," he said. "I don't think they're going to go away."

item.title: Lindblad and Lawson to continue at Racing Bulls
item.description: Arvid Lindblad (left) and Liam Lawson have taken Racing Bulls to fifth place in the constructors' championship on 114 points, 45 points ahead of Alpine [Getty Images] Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson will continue as the drivers for Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls in 2027. Red Bull had been deciding whether to promote Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov in place of Lawson but have decided to spend a second season assessing their current line-up Tsolov will be the reserve driver for both teams next season. Team principal Alan Permane said: "I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing." The decision to retain both marks a break from the previous Red Bull philosophy of fast-tracking drivers through the programme. Chequered Flag Extra: The Making of Kimi Antonelli Racing Bulls essentially exists to find potential drivers for the main Red Bull team, so the company has tended to jettison drivers who have been given a chance and not succeeded. That's why Lawson, 24, was considered vulnerable. He was promoted to Red Bull alongside Max Verstappen for the 2025 season only to be demoted after just two races in which he had struggled. The New Zealander has since sought to rebuild his career and was much more convincing when he was re-promoted to Red Bull for the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix this year while regular driver Isack Hadjar was recovering from a broken wrist. Keeping Lawson on board for 2027 gives Red Bull a known-quality benchmark with which to continue their assessment of Lindblad, who made his debut this season. The 19-year-old Briton has excelled at times in his rookie year but on average has been a little behind Lawson, who has out-qualified him 13 times to nine and has scored more than twice as many points. Lawson said: "We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving. "It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for fifth place in the constructors' championship. "I'm looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I'm excited by what we can achieve together." Lindblad added: "It's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test. I'd like to thank everyone for their trust and support. "I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season." The news release announcing the pairing made no mention of Tsolov, who is expected to be retained by Red Bull in some form of reserve role in which he gains experience through work in the simulator and with testing previous cars. item.title: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst
item.description: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick secured a third-place finish and helped Manchester United return to the Champions League. However, the club’s hierarchy ruined all the momentum during the summer transfer window, overseeing a botched-up midfield rebuild and overlooking their abysmal defence. The defeat against Hull City in the Premier League opener teased what was to come, and the outburst following the loss at Atlético Madrid highlighted that Carrick is no longer in control of the ship. Jason Wilcox reprimanded Lisandro Martínez Manchester United’s first real test in the Champions League after nearly a three-year absence came against Atlético Madrid. A goal in the very first minute in the Spanish capital underlined the gulf between United and Europe’s elite. The Red Devils spent most of the night ball-watching or ball-chasing, saw Leny Yoro get sent off, and conceded another. Lisandro Martinez chose to show his intensity off the pitch, as he launched a “blistering tirade” at Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, and INEOS over their transfer business. The Argentine was not wrong, but that certainly was not the right place to air behind-the-scenes frustrations. According to The Telegraph , Martínez was fined and apologised publicly and is thought to have been given a serious dressing-down in private by Wilcox over the rant. “Martínez was put in his place,” one source told the publication. The Telegraph added that several people internally felt that the outburst was rich coming from a player who had spent so much time on the sidelines since signing in 2022 and, in the words of one source, was “playing abysmally” and pointed to his contractual situation. Signed from Ajax, the Argentina international is out of contract at United next summer and is expected to depart. Dressing room without leaders The report claims that around the time of that Atlético defeat there were “growing doubts among the first-team staff about whether they could halt the slide.” There was concern that United’s squad was “badly lacking not just in terms of physicality, pace and aggression, but also natural leaders and players with aura and presence.” A week later, United proved their doubters right by succumbing to a 4–1 defeat to Como, who were playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history. According to the report, after this match, it was Bruno Fernandes’ turn to show the world that Carrick’s project is on the brink of collapsing, as the captain publicly questioned the head coach’s approach. He was subsequently dropped to the bench against Bournemouth, who beat the Red Devils 3–0 at Old Trafford.

item.title: Miami Heat’s Vice City Jerseys Are The Ultimate GTA VI Flex
item.description: Credit: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images The Miami Heat did not just release new jerseys, according to Sports Illustrated . They launched a full-scale event tied to the biggest video game launch in history. Grand Theft Auto VI drops on November 19th, and the team is ready to match that energy. The Heat will debut special-edition Vice City kits the night before the game starts. This happens when they face the Milwaukee Bucks. Outlaw Vibes on the Court Keshad Johnson knows exactly what this means for the fans. He grew up sneaking away to play the game in Oakland. “It caused some fights between me and him on turns,” Johnson says about his brother Kenny. The new uniforms capture that same feeling. They are all black with bright pink accents that look like neon signs. Hidden inside the letters and numbers is a map of Miami streets. Johnson called the look an “outlaw type vibe” in an interview with GQ. That is the exact feeling the team wants to project. The jerseys were designed by Nike and Travis Scott’s Cactus Jack brand. Their logos appear on both the shirts and the shorts. Details like these show the franchise is serious about this crossover. “My whole family is trying to get a Vice City jersey,” Johnson said when we spoke last weekend. Jennifer Alvarez, the Miami Heat Chief Creative Officer, sees the bigger picture. “We’re bringing sports and entertainment together in a way that’s never been done,” she told GQ. She added that the team aims to deliver an experience no one has had at an NBA game before. This is not just a uniform swap. It is a total immersion into the game’s world. Bringing Vice City to Life The Kaseya Center will transform into the video game itself. The plaza will feature a light-blue Ferrari and a turquoise Chevrolet Monte Carlo. These are just two of the cars players can drive in the game. A large sign on top of the arena will read “Welcome to Vice City.” The effort required to build this setup is massive. The helicopter was there to help install the sign. Fans attending the game on Wednesday night can buy the jerseys at the arena. They can also order burgers from Burger Shot. This is a rare chance to step inside a fictional world that feels real. The Heat are betting that Miami fans will embrace this connection. Johnson noted that the city has its own fashion culture. Bam Adebayo agrees that Vice City has a unique style. The Heat are leaning into that local identity while tapping into a global gaming audience. Now, only Rockstar Games and the Heat can pull off the event. The game launches on November 19th, but the celebration starts the night before.

item.title: From Talking Drums to Tourism Diplomacy: How Nigeria Captured Attention at WTM London 2026
item.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing. Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world. It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it. Day Two: Tourism, Tradition and Private Sector Connections The second day combined cultural discovery with industry engagement, featuring a traditional palm wine experience, networking and interactions between Nigerian tourism stakeholders and international visitors. An important part of Nigeria’s participation was the presence of the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA), one of the foremost voices of Nigeria’s organised travel trade. NANTA’s participation celebrated the longstanding contribution of Nigerian travel professionals to the country

item.title: Michigan State vs. Washington: Score predictions, analysis from Spartans Wire staff
item.description: Can Michigan State football make it back-to-back wins for the first time since the opening weeks of the season? The Spartans Wire crew believes that's possible. Michigan State football will look to build off last week's monstrous rivalry win over Michigan in a home afternoon matchup against Washington. The Spartans come into this game looking to keep bowl eligibility alive with a victory over the Huskies . Michigan State enters this game sitting at 3-6 overall and 1-5 in Big Ten play. The victory over the Wolverines last week snapped a six-game losing streak. Washington is looking to bounce back from a tough home loss against Penn State last weekend. The Huskies are 5-4 overall and 2-4 in Big Ten play this season. Kickoff for this game is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET from Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. This game will be televised on the Big Ten Network. Let's take a look at our predictions for this week's matchup between Michigan State and Washington below: Andrew Brewster Prediction: Michigan State 17, Washington 14 Saturday felt like a shift for this MSU program. After a season of missed opportunities, narrow losses, and frustrating games, the Spartans finally broke through with a win over Michigan on the road. The defense played lights out, and the offense was able to sustain drives, despite some continued red zone issues. I think Spartan Stadium will be rocking on Saturday and MSU can win this game. Cory Linsner Prediction: Michigan State 23, Washington 21 The up-down theory feels like it could sneak its head into this game, with Michigan State coming off of the biggest win of its season, and Washington suffering a gross home loss to Penn State. I'm going to bet on the Spartans culture and maturity here, while Washington seems to be struggling in that category. Robert Bondy Prediction: Michigan State 23, Washington 20 Michigan State is primed for a letdown spot after the stunning rivalry win last week. But last week's win and the way Michigan State has been building up to that game makes it feel different to me. I'm with Andrew that I believe last week wasn't a one-off performance and we are going to see the Spartans build off it instead of living off the win. I have this as a tight game, with Michigan State coming through late to get the narrow win over the Huskies. Contact/Follow us @ The SpartansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Michigan State news, notes and opinion. You can also follow Robert Bondy on X @ RobertBondy5 . This article originally appeared on Spartans Wire: Michigan State vs. Washington: Score predictions, analysis from Spartans Wire staff

item.title: Fall Ball Is Over: What Did We Learn About WVU Baseball?
item.description: Well, fall ball is officially over, which means we are one step closer to WVU baseball being back. And honestly, after the season the Mountaineers had last year, I am already ready for February. WVU is coming off a pretty impressive season, finishing with 47 wins and making it all the way to Omaha for the first time in program history. Not bad, right? But as exciting as last season was, this year’s team is going to look a little different. Head coach Steve Sabins has some new faces to work with, some important players to replace and some pretty high expectations heading into 2027. So, now that fall ball is over, what did we learn? The new guys could bring some serious power One thing that stood out to me was the potential WVU has at the plate this season. Sabins recently talked about newcomers Colin Coonradt and Ryan Piekutoski, who combined for around 60 home runs at the junior college level last season. And that is a lot of home runs. Now, obviously, playing in the Big 12 is going to be a little different, but I think it is pretty exciting to see what these two could bring to the lineup. Last season, WVU was really good at being aggressive on the bases, and now it looks like the Mountaineers could have some extra power to go along with that. And if these guys can adjust to Big 12 pitching, I think WVU’s offense could be pretty fun to watch. There is still plenty of experience coming back Even with all the changes, WVU still has some pretty important players returning. Gavin Kelly is back after hitting .382 with 19 home runs and 63 RBIs last season, which is obviously a pretty big deal. Armani Guzman, Tyrus Hall and Matt Ineich are also returning, giving WVU some familiar faces to build around. And I think that is going to be really important. These guys know what it takes to win, and they have already experienced playing on one of the biggest stages in college baseball. But WVU is also replacing five spots in its lineup, so there is still a lot to figure out before the season starts. I think it will be interesting to see which newcomers step up and how Sabins puts everything together. The pitching staff still has some questions Now, this is probably one of the biggest things I am interested in heading into the season. WVU lost some important pitchers, including Maxx Yehl, Dawson Montesa and Ian Korn. And replacing those guys is not going to be easy. The Mountaineers have plenty of arms to work with, but figuring out who takes over those roles is going to be pretty important. Who’s going to be in the starting rotation? Who’s going to step up out of the bullpen? Those are things we still do not really know. Sabins has talked about evaluating his players throughout the fall, so I think the next few months are going to be important for figuring out what the pitching staff will look like. There is definitely talent there, but we will have to wait and see how it all comes together. There is still a lot to figure out One thing that became pretty clear

item.title: 49ers bold predictions review: How August takes look in November
item.description: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Back in August, before the season started, I dropped my four bold predictions for the 2026 San Francisco 49ers. I am personally a fan of accountability, so while bold predictions are meant to be a little wild and out there, I wanted to go back and see just how close I was. Hold myself accountable, you know? And while I feel good about some, others I feel less than good about. Let’s make a midseason critique of my pre-season bold predictions: The 49ers go 6-0 against the NFC West I feel so good about this that I don’t really consider this one a bold prediction anymore for two reasons: The 49ers are the best team in the division (which could have been expected before the season started) and The Rams and Seahawks aren’t great (something that wasn’t expected). The 49ers are halfway to a perfect divisional record, and the two toughest games are already out of the way. San Francisco easily disposed of the Rams in Australia in Week 1 and then pulled a close one out over the Seahawks in Seattle in Week 5. Sandwiched between those two was a one-possession win over Arizona in Week 3. Oddly enough, with Seattle and the Rams still on the schedule, the toughest battle for perfection might be the last with that Week 18 game in Arizona. If the 49ers can continue to have the grip on the NFC West they have right now, it’s possible San Francisco would have nothing to play for in this game and give the starters a rest (and maybe some gamesmanship to worsen Arizona’s draft position). Of all the preseason bold predictions, this is the one I feel best about. Mike Evans sets a career-high in receptions I still can’t believe Evans has never had 100 receptions in a season. 11 seasons in a row with at least 1,000 receiving yards, but never once triple-digit receptions. Amazing. And while Evans has clearly been the 49ers’ No. 1 receiver, this one will fall short for two reasons: His 4.5 receptions per game in his six games played would come out to 76-77 receptions over the 17-game season. Silly of me to expect a triple-digit reception season from a 49ers offense that loves to spread the ball around. The whole Achilles injury thing has me concerned about the next time we will even see Evans play. Even though he won’t set a career-high in receptions, it is easy to see the impact Evans has had on the 49ers offense. Once Evans gets back to playing shape, him playing alongside Keenan Allen could make for an even more explosive offense. Jack Jones leads the 49ers in interceptions Can’t win them all. Sometimes you have to go to Atlanta for an early game right before the bye week. But I guess we aren’t completely dead, as the 49ers brought Jones back to the practice squad on Wednesday. Shout out, Renardo Green. Maxx Crosby will be a 49er at some point I am frustrated by the 49ers’ trade deadline. I think they did a good job with who they acquired. item.title: Ashton Jeanty struggles in both running and receiving game in Week 9
item.description: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-17 loss at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick saw his play time increase after he played a career low 40 percent of the snaps in Week 8. Jeanty played 64 percent of the snaps at San Francisco. Yet, his production remained low. Jeanty had 25 yards on six carries. He has 98 yards rushing on 36 carries in the past five games. Jeanty has been effective as a receiver, but not in Week 9. He has five catches for minus-5 yards Sunday. Jack Bech: The second-round pick played 17 snaps, he fewest in a game this season he finished healthy. He had one catch for nine yards on two targets. Bech has six catches for 57 yards in five games this season. Darien Porter: The third-round pick played 52 percent of the snaps and started after he missed almost all of Week 8 with a groin injury. Caleb Rogers: The benched starter finished the game when he replaced rookie Trey Zuhn at right guard in the third quarter. Zuhn has a concussion and he could miss the Seattle game. Thus, Rogers, a third-round pick, could start this week. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense as usual. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, has been on the 53-man roster for two games and he was inactive for both games. Not great. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 33 snaps, the fourth most by Raiders’ defensive tackles against the 49ers. He had been the leading snap getter at the position most of the season. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the fourth time this season. He played 13 defensive snaps. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 18 snaps on special teams, which is his norm. He has played just three defensive snaps this season.

item.title: 5 things to know about Northwestern
item.description: EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 17: Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) walks off the field with offensive coordinator Chip Kelly following a college football game between the Michigan State Spartans and Northwestern Wildcats on October 17, 2026 at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The No. 20 Ohio State Buckeyes (6-3, 4-2) will host the Northwestern Wildcats (6-3, 3-3) and former offensive coordinator Chip Kelly as they attempt to get back on track following back-to-back losses to USC and Oregon. Here are five things to know about Northwestern. Aidan Chiles is out For the second straight week, Northwestern starting quarterback Aidan Chiles will be out due to an injury. Chiles has been great for the Wildcats this year, and has been a large part of their success. The Oregon State and Michigan State transfer has thrown for 1,898 yards, 13 touchdowns, and just one interception this season, while running for 274 more yards and 10 touchdowns. Nicco Marchiol started for the Wildcats against Iowa, and should be line to start on Saturday. Chip Kelly returns Chip Kelly returns to Columbus as the Northwestern offensive coordinator after winning the 2024 national championship as the Ohio State offensive coordinator. After Ohio State, Kelly went to the Las Vegas Raiders, but was fired the same season he was hired. He made his way to Northwestern and has been fantastic. In 2024, Ohio State averaged 37.2 points and 429.4 total yards per game. In 2026, Northwestern averages 33.6 points and 438.1 yards per game. Griffin Wilde is a game-changer There are a lot of great receivers in the Big Ten, and Griffin Wilde for Northwestern is certainly one of them. Wilde has 49 catches for 813 yards and five touchdowns this season and is averaging 16.6 yards per catch. In his career with South Dakota State and Northwestern, he has 211 catches for 3,246 yards and 31 touchdowns. It will take a great effort from the Ohio State secondary to keep him in front all game and slow him down. Ryan Field is no more (at least the stadium) While this game is in Columbus, Northwestern has a new home this season, and it has made waves in the college football world. A new stadium opened using the same name, and is a huge upgrade for the Wildcats. On Sept. 22, 2021, Northwestern announced that the Ryan family had donated $480 million to the university to replace Ryan Field with a new stadium at the existing site. The university estimated it would bring a $1.3 billion economic impact to the Chicago area, including $659 million in economic impact to Evanston. The 34-game losing streak Northwestern lays claim to one of the longest losing streaks in college football history. In the early 1980s, the football team suffered a historic 34-game losing streak from 1979 to 1982. As of right now, this is still the longest losing streak in college football history. Virginia is second at 28, from 1958 to 1

item.title: Penn State holds key advantages over Minnesota’s defense
item.description: Penn State’s offense is officially fun to watch again. The unit has put together back-to-back strong performances — although it hit a lull in the second half last week — against the Purdue Boilermakers and Washington Huskies . The most exciting part about the scoring uptick is that it has happened without wide receiver Koby Howard . Quarterback Rocco Becht finally looks comfortable playing against Big Ten competition, and it has paid off in a big way for the Nittany Lions . However, they won’t have a cakewalk this week, as Minnesota has one of the better defenses in the conference. It only allows 20.5 points per game, and it is just below the Nittany Lions in terms of yardage allowed, currently giving up 305 yards per game. Let’s compare Penn State’s offense to Minnesota’s defense and see who has the edge. Yards per carry Penn State offense: 4.15 yards per carry Minnesota defense: 3.88 yards per carry These numbers suggest that the blue and white have a mediocre running game and Minnesota has an excellent run defense. However, the Nittany Lions have been running the ball much more effectively lately, and they could pose a threat this weekend. Penn State’s running backs have been averaging 6.2 yards per carry over the last two games. The rushes have been much more explosive, and the running backs are finding yards more consistently in the power running game. This type of balance between the run and the pass could give the team an advantage going into Week 11. Time of possession Penn State offense: 32 minutes Minnesota defense: 29 minutes These two teams have nearly identical average times of possession. This could mean that whoever is able to establish the run and control the game will have a strong chance of winning. We just saw Penn State own the time of possession battle against Purdue a couple of weeks ago, and it resulted in a 31-17 victory that felt a lot bigger than what the scoreboard suggested. It’ll be hard to get to 43 minutes of possession again, but keeping Minnesota’s defense on the field will be key. Fourth-down conversions Penn State offense: 77.8% conversion rate Minnesota defense: allow 55.6% conversion rate The fourth-down battle is something Penn State should always have the edge in, as it converts 77.8% of its attempts. The Nittany Lions have been great at converting these short-yardage situations, and it really helps to give the offense second and third chances to stay on the field. Conversely, the Golden Gophers struggle with stopping teams on fourth down. Getting an extra set of downs when you would have normally punted also keeps your offense on the field longer, circling back to the time of possession battle. If Penn State wins this area of the game, then it can kill two birds with one stone. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . This article originally appeared on Nittany Lions Wire: Penn State holds key advantages over Minnesota’s defense

item.title: Ravens add failed Rams kicker to new kicking competition
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Ravens add failed Rams kicker to new kicking competition appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens have been busy making kicker moves of late. After placing Tyler Loop on injured reserve, the Ravens went with Jake Moody for Thursday night’s 33-10 loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars . However, he has since signed with the Atlanta Falcons. The Ravens signed Riley Patterson to their 53-man roster to fill the void left by Moody. And As NFL inside Ian Rapoport reported, they also added former Los Angeles Rams kicker Harrison Mevis to the practice squad as added competition for Patterson. Mevis, who is known as the “Thiccer Kicker,” played nine games for the Rams last season, converting 12 of 13 field goal attempts as a rookie. However, he suffered a significant sophomore slump as he missed four of nine field goal attempts in five games this season. The Rams finally cut the cord on him after he went 0-of-2 in a 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills last month. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mevis now joins a Ravens team whose season has completely gone off the rails amid disastrous collapses and crippling quarterback injuries. They’ve lost four games in a row while losing their top two quarterbacks, Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, to season-ending injuries. Baltimore traded for veteran QB Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. He will now take over as the starter for Week 10, replacing rookie Joe Fagnano, who started on Thursday night against the Jaguars. The snake-bitten Ravens will have a golden opportunity to end their losing skid as they take on the still-winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. item.title: Chargers’ 2026 NFL trade deadline is now a tragically epic failure after Daiyan Henley debacle
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Chargers’ 2026 NFL trade deadline is now a tragically epic failure after Daiyan Henley debacle appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 NFL season has been an absolute disaster for the Los Angeles Chargers . LA is 0-8 on the season and looks in danger of being the first 0-17 team in NFL history. The NFL trade deadline was not much better for the Chargers. LA took a delusional approach to the deadline , only coming around on being sellers at the absolute last minute. The Chargers did attempt to make one deadline trade , but even that went horribly wrong. LA agreed to terms to send Daiyan Henley to Denver. However, the Broncos released a statement early Thursday morning announcing that the Henley deal was off . It is an understatement to say that LA’s approach to the deadline was a complete mistake. But the Henley trade shows just how much LA’s leadership screwed the whole thing up. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why did the Daiyan Henley trade fall apart? Both the Chargers and Broncos have confirmed that the trade is off. However, neither team is publicly talking about why the deal did not happen. At this point, it is unclear if those details will ever see the light of day. NFL insiders could gain more information about the situation and report on it, but there’s no guarantee that happens. The Chargers lost out on some significant assets when this trade fell apart. LA was set to gain a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for the veteran linebacker. Those selections could have been useful pieces for rebuilding the roster, which seems destined to happen this offseason. Regardless, the bigger lesson here is that LA shouldn’t have waited until the last minute to do their business. The Chargers should have been more aggressive ahead of the NFL trade deadline The Henley trade falling apart is bad, but it could’ve been survivable if only they’d had more time to negotiate. Or at least find another trade partner for Henley’s services. LA’s 0-8 record did not sneak up on the team. The Chargers have been in freefall for weeks and a fire sale seemed like an inevitability . Unfortunately, Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers held onto hope for far too long and missed their opportunity to sell assets. Now the Chargers are stuck with multiple veterans on expiring contracts who could easily walk away this spring. Players like Henley, Khalil Mack, and Tuli Tuipulotu were not moved at the deadline. Now the best the Chargers can hope for is gaining a few compensatory picks in future seasons. The Chargers also shot down a Ladd McConkey trade . That is another missed opportunity, though it makes sense to keep McConkey if they did not receive a blockbuster offer. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has quiet 4th quarter in OKC's loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: Surrounded by three defenders, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander contorted his slender frame to get by. He took one dribble as he crouched down near the floor. Taking an off-balance floater, he hurled the ball at the rim. It banked in. The circus shot sadly represented his sole fourth-quarter bucket. The Oklahoma City Thunder failed in crunch time in a 118-108 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers . They leave Moda Center humbled at what their glued-together squad's ceiling is. Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 31 points on 9-of-20 shooting, four rebounds and two assists. He shot 0-of-7 from 3 and went 13-of-14 on free throws. He also had one steal. I will say this — before I criticize his night — Gilgeous-Alexander's frustrating games are an efficient 30 points. There's a level of hilarious absurdity there. Goes to show what the standard is for one of the era-defining NBA superstars of the 2020s. Now that that's been stated. Man, the Thunder just need more out of the 28-year-old. Preferably, the playstyle that helped him become a two-time MVP winner. Right now, OKC is getting a bare-bones version of that. It was a tale of two halves for Gilgeous-Alexander. Or, to be more accurate, three frustrating quarters and one strong frame. The shot process has been off-kilter all year. The drives to the rim are way down. So are the free-throw numbers. The 28-year-old has absolutely fallen in love with contested mid-range and outside jumpers. Right now, that's not what the Thunder need. They don't have the luxury of experimentation or have feel-out stints. He needs to be on the pedal to the metal at all times. The first half was the antithesis of that. Gilgeous-Alexander had eight points on 3-of-11 shooting. Yuck. The shot chart painted an uglier picture. It's almost like he's purposely avoiding getting inside the paint. If you feel like I'm being too harsh, then he likely had the same thought process at the break. The second half was a return to form. Gilgeous-Alexander went back to his vintage form. A bunch of drives to the rim and pulling up in the mid-range. The Trail Blazers had zero answers. He had 16 points in the third frame. He attacked on every touch he had. That helped him put up a bloated night from the free-throw line. It was a nice throwback to his last few years of how he'd usually racked up super-efficient 30-point outings. Sadly, that only lasted there. Gilgeous-Alexander was quiet in the fourth quarter. He only had seven points. Mostly on free throws, too. Regardless of how you want to slice up the blame pie, that can't happen. Especially in these circumstances, where OKC is without four of its best five players. There's no justifying a quiet closeout like that. The Thunder need him to cut out his bad habits of settling for contested jumpers and fading into the background at times.
