item.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Quarterback Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Jordan Love vs. C.J. Stroud
item.description: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) looks to throw against the Los Angeles Chargers during the third quarter at SoFi Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jordan Love and C.J. Stroud have been balling at the QB position this season, giving fantasy football managers plenty of positive performances. While both Love and Stroud face stiffer matchups in Week 10, there's a good chance many managers are still starting them. Between Love and Stroud, which QB is the better fantasy football starter in Week 10? All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros . Jordan Love Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) drops back to pass against the New England Patriots in the second half at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Entering Week 10, Love is the QB4 in fantasy points per game (21.2). In Week 9 against the New England Patriots, Love produced a season-best 36.2 fantasy points. Jordan Love leads the league in passing yards pic.twitter.com/fH6gYDiLZk - ESPN Fantasy Sports (@ESPNFantasy) November 11, 2026 Not many QBs have been playing better than Love, who has the seventh-most yards per attempt (7.7), the third-most passing touchdowns (19), and the sixth-lowest pressure-to-sack rate (12.5%) among the 21 QBs with 250-plus dropbacks. Up next for Love is a daunting Minnesota Vikings defense that he scored 20.5 fantasy points against in Week 1. C.J. Stroud Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) runs with the ball against the Los Angeles Chargers during the third quarter at SoFi Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Only Stroud scored more fantasy points (36.4) than Love in Week 9, tossing five touchdowns against the Los Angeles Chargers. Across his first eight starts in 2026, Stroud is the QB6 in fantasy points per game (20.8). CJ STROUD LEGACY GAME 352 PASS YARDS 5 PASS TD 124.0 PASS RATING pic.twitter.com/6OaHIFOqBL - PFF (@PFF) November 8, 2026 In the same QB sample from above, Stroud has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.0), the sixth-most passing touchdowns (16), and the eighth-lowest pressure-to-sack rate (14.2%). While Love has Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, Stroud has an assortment of capable pass-catchers alongside Nico Collins . Final Verdict: Start C.J. Stroud Although I'd be comfortable starting both Love and Stroud in Week 10, Stroud gets the slight nod with the Cleveland Browns' defense being a bit more fantasy-friendly. The Vikings are permitting the fewest schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to QBs (-8.8), while the Browns are giving up the 10th-fewest (-1.1). Additionally, Minnesota's defense ranks 1st in pressure rate (45.6%), compared to Cleveland's defense being 10th (37.9%). Given the matchups and the fact that Stroud won't be blitzed on nearly every play, the Texans' signal-caller is in a better spot than Love if deciding between the two talented QBs. item.title: The replicants are running the city in thrilling final trailer for ‘Blade Runner 2099’ (video)
item.description: null One of the most anticipated fall TV series, " Blade Runner 2099 , " recently dropped its final neon-tinted trailer, and now we’ve finally got a handle on the plot dynamics of this dystopian thriller set in the cyberpunk world of Ridley Scott's original. Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens. "In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis. "To secure a stable future for her brother, she assumes one final identity and is forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who’s confronting the end of her life. The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn." This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight! "You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop. Will "Blade Runner 2099" usher in a new era for the sci-fi franchise? (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099 " sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Delivered by creator and showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls"), and executive produced by Silka Louisa and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" lands on Prime Video beginning Nov. 25, 2026 .

item.title: How to College Football: Week 11
item.description: The race for the final conference championship games is nearing its finish. Below Division 1, this is the last week of the season for most teams as they begin the push for their respective playoffs. Let’s jump in. Also, the FBS rankings below are based on the CFP rankings this time. Thursday There are two games on tonight, but I only have things to say about the first one. 7:00 p.m. on ESPN: Memphis at South Florida Memphis needs to win this to keep their American Conference Championship Game hopes alive, while USF is still trying to figure out how to do any sort of offense. If Charles Huff can get to the title game, he might get poached to another job and become the first FBS coach to helm four teams in four years. 8:00 p.m. on ESPN2: 62 nd Battle on the Bayou (ULL at ULM) Friday There are four games tonight in D1. I will talk about the FBS games. 6:00 p.m. on ESPN: Florida State at Pitt Neither of these teams are that good, but FSU needs to win two of their next three games to get to bowl eligibility. It’s unlikely they take a bowl bid if they earn one, but it’d feel slightly better than a losing season. 8:00 p.m. on Fox: Illinois at #4 UCLA This should be an easy UCLA win thanks to Illinois being in a funk. They’re three wins away from locking up a spot in the B1G Championship Game and playing for a chance at their first conference title since 1998. What an incredible first year. 9:00 p.m. on ESPN+: Southern Utah at Portland State 9:15 p.m. on ESPN: #14 Houston at Colorado Being ranked 14 th in the CFP’s latest poll gives Houston hope at making the tournament without needing to go to Arlington. A win at Colorado is obviously a requirement for such a miracle, and they’ve had their moments of competence. Saturday morning You’ll have to wait until later for the ranked teams to really kick into gear, but there are still good games worth watching at 11 a.m. Fox: Northwestern at #20 Ohio State Oh no, Ohio State is having a bad season. Bad means three losses for these people. Have no sympathy and laugh at them. I hope Northwestern goes in there and runs CFL plays on them en route to a massive victory. Fun fact, Northwestern hasn’t won in Columbus since 1971 and has only won two of their last 40 match-ups in this series. ABC: Duke at #7 Miami (FL) This game will feature perhaps the best player in college football, and it’s not a Hurricane. Duke sophomore RB Nate Sheppard, a graduate of Mandeville High School in Louisiana, is a Maxwell Award finalist and one of the most dynamic players in the country. He has a nation-high 21 total TDs, a school-record 17 rushing TDs, and over 1500 all-purpose yards. Miami should win, but if he shines, he might win the Heisman. ESPN: #13 Wake Forest at SMU Playoff Wake Forest would be amazing, and a win in this game gets the Demon Deacons one step closer. item.title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Protector of the Year
item.description: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. So far, we’ve awarded: Most Improved Player : DB Chris Roland-Wallace Top Defensive Rookie : CB Mansoor Delane In this post, we’ll reveal our top offensive lineman so far . RG Trey Smith VOTING: Trey Smith (5), Kahlil Benson (2), Creed Humphrey (2) The NFL now gives out the “Protector of the Year” award, so we will too. Right guard Trey Smith is the winner at the midseason point, playing 506 of 510 possible snaps and starting in all eight games. The Chiefs’ run game has been revitalized this year, and Smith has been a key factor in the push up front. Kansas City ranks 10th in ESPN’s run-block win rate (74%), despite two games in which starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched. The Chiefs rank 12th in pass-block win rate as a unit, and Smith does not grade as highly in pass blocking as Humphrey or Suamataia, according to ESPN , but Smith has allowed just seven pressures (two quarterback hits and five hurries) over 307 pass-blocking snaps; Suamataia has allowed seven pressures (one sack, three hits and three pressures) in just 221 pass-blocking snaps, according to Pro Football Focus . The intensity Smith brings is the cherry on top of his reliable presence on the line. He isn’t a perfect blocker, but he’s been Kansas City’s most consistent offensive lineman in a season where the unit’s depth is already being tested. Center Creed Humphrey’s low snaps likely hurt his chances at winning the poll, but rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson deserved some love; he has played every snap possible at left tackle this season. Is Smith the Chiefs’ top offensive lineman so far this year? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Seahawks All-22 review: What the film tells us from Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Cardinals
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks catches a pass in front of Baron Browning #5 of the Arizona Cardinals during the first half at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks bounced back from their loss to the Chicago Bears, defeating the Arizona Cardinals at home to move back above .500. Beating Arizona wasn’t enough to restore all the confidence Seattle had lost or completely revive its playoff hopes. Still, with seven players ruled out, including Sam Darnold, Quenton Nelson, Charles Cross, Leonard Williams, Uchenna Nwosu and Rashid Shaheed, this was a game the Seahawks simply could not afford to lose. Despite facing an opponent that never looked particularly threatening, Seattle showed resilience and, more importantly, a few signs of improvement. The 17-3 victory wasn’t spectacular , but there were encouraging developments on both sides of the ball. Let’s take a look at the good, the bad, and what the All-22 tells us about Seattle’s performance. The Bad The offensive line still has a long way to go The Seahawks’ offensive line continues to struggle with consistency. Injuries certainly haven’t helped, and the anticipated impact of Quenton Nelson’s arrival has been delayed by a few weeks. Grey Zabel vs Quenton Nelson execution pic.twitter.com/lSXXC3T8Kg — Alexandre Castro (@alexcastrofilho) November 11, 2026 Speaking of Nelson, there was plenty of discussion about whether Anthony Bradford should remain in the starting lineup while Grey Zabel moved to the bench once Nelson returned. I think this game provided another reason why that shouldn’t happen. Bradford’s limitations remain evident, while Zabel still offers considerably more long-term upside. Here, Bradford’s immediate loss in pass protection (on the game’s first play, nonetheless) prevents Drew Lock from getting to any secondary reads. He’s easily beaten by Walter Nolen’s hand technique and has no opportunity to recover once the pressure gets through. You might argue that Bradford isn’t particularly good in pass protection, but at least he contributes to the running game. That’s true to some extent, but his run blocking has been far from consistent. He was thoroughly dominated by Walter Nolen and Andrew Billings throughout the game. On this play, his poor timing and angle leave the defensive tackle free to blow up the entire run. That doesn’t mean Zabel has been playing particularly well, either. I simply believe his potential is considerably higher than anything Bradford has shown so far. On this snap, Zabel fails to properly set up his pull block, missing the opportunity to create space and ultimately blowing up the play. Abe Lucas also hasn’t returned to his previous level of play. On this snap, he’s beaten by LJ Collier. There’s not much more to explain here: it’s simply a bad rep from the right tackle. As mentioned earlier, this isn’t a problem isolated to

item.title: Syracuse Men’s Soccer: Orange face undefeated SMU in ACC Semifinal
item.description: CARY, NC - DECEMBER 12: Head coach Ian McIntyre of Syracuse University poses for a photo with Atlantic Coast Conference commissioner Jim Phillips after winning the 2022 Men's College Cup Final between Indiana and Syracuse at Sahlen's Stadium at WakeMed Soccer Park on December 12, 2022 in Cary, North Carolina. (Photo by Andy Mead/ISI Photos/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange men’s soccer team travels to Cary, NC to face SMU in the ACC tournament semifinal tonight at 8:30 pm. The game will be broadcast on ACC Network. The Orange reached the semifinal round after a 2-1 win over Stanford in double overtime. The game started out very slow, as there were no goals for the first 85 minutes of the match. Then, late fireworks came with a Syracuse corner, which, after a shot from Kristjan Fortier was parried by the keeper, Jordan Grey was able to tap in to put the Orange up 1-0 with five minutes to play. The excitement was short-lived, however, as an incredible outside-the-box strike from Stanford would level the match just a minute later. It would take two overtime periods to decide this one, however, as Jordan Grey would get the ball around midfield, fend off two defenders on a solo run to goal, and place the ball just under the arm of Stanford’s keeper to move the Orange on to Cary for the fourth time in five seasons. Awaiting them is the SMU Mustangs, who have been by far the ACC’s best this season. The Mustangs are currently ranked as the #1 team in the nation and have not lost a game so far, although they do have three draws. To get here, they battered Virginia 6-0, which is a team the Orange drew 1-1. SMU is a great team that is seemingly heating up at the right time, and the Orange will certainly have their work cut out for them if they want to make the ACC Final. Syracuse’s defense has continued to be the star of the show during the Orange’s surprise ACC tournament run. They’ve held both opponents they’ve faced to only one goal, and against Stanford, the Cardinal were only able to get six total shots off, with the only one they had on goal being the one they scored from, as well as only getting a single shot off in both overtime periods. The Orange attack, which is a unit that has struggled this season, has not had to do much; however, they have scored in their last four games. If you take out these last four matches, the Orange have only scored twice all season. Their three tournament goals are also dangerously close to their four regular-season ACC goals this season. SMU as a team is good at everything; They are second in the conference in goals scored with 18 in the regular season, and have given up the fewest goals in the conference with two. In terms of the entire country, SMU is fourth in total goals scored, with at least one fewer game played than all the teams ahead of them, and ranks first in the entire country in fewest goals allowed, with six total in 16 matches. There’s a reason why this team is the number one team in the

item.title: 2026 Phillies report cards: Jonathan Bowlan
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Jonathan Bowlan #52 of the Philadelphia Phillies reacts on the mound with teammate Alec Bohm #28 prior to leaving a game against the New York Mets in the eighth inning at Citi Field on September 17, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dave Dombrowski has done a lot of good things with the Phillies, the best being the ability to convince John Middleton to open his wallet for free agents. Some of his signings have stunk, but some have been quietly solid. Where he has struggled though is building a consistently good bullpen that will get the team from quality starts to victories. Once he traded for Jhoan Duran, he got himself a top notch end of game piece that locks down games for them, but he still needed some bridges to get to Duran. He had some, like Jose Alvarado and Matt Strahm, but once Strahm was up for arbitration, they moved on from him in a trade. The player he acquired, Jonathan Bowlan, had a strong season in his first for the Phillies. Is there anything more that he can tap into? 2026 stats: 59 G, 56 1/3 IP, 31.9 K%, 6.6 BB%, 1.28 HR/9, 47.8 GB%, 3.36 ERA (3.37 FIP) What went right Bowlan was quite the find this year for the Phillies, eventually becoming their second most trusted reliever as the season wore on. That title belonged to Brad Keller at the beginning of the year, but the combination of the injury to Keller and effective pitching by Bowlan elevated him in the pecking order. He used a hard, riding fastball to establish himself at the top of the zone quite well. Compared to league average, it had more “ride” than the rest of the league, which was surprising. He used that ride with velocity that hit triple digits a few times to get on top of hitters, complementing it with a slider that was a hard breaker down and away to righties, sent to the backfoot on lefties. He did all the things one wants a reliever to do: induce swing and miss, keep the ball on the ground (mostly) and be able to get outs on his own without relying on a leaky defense. What went wrong The biggest obstacle for Bowlan looked to be himself. He just wore down at the end of the year. Consider that on September 2, after his outing the night before, Bowlan had a nice ERA of 2.82 with peripherals and back of the baseball card numbers that looked just as good. Then, in his next five outings, he allowed a home run and was sent to the injured list for a breather. When you struggled to earn the trust of a manager like Mattingly, gaining that trust back is difficult if there is an injury holding him back, but the playoff inning he threw looked like that trust was basically evaporated. Final grade: B+ One of the major criticisms of Don Mattingly was his usage of the bullpen. Towards, the end of the season, there were only two relievers that he actually trusted, Bowlan being one of them, Jhoan Duran being the other. With Duran, there was not much of a time where he was warmed up without the intention

item.title: Xabi Alonso can miss out on top five and still keep his job claims journalist
item.description: Xabi Alonso can miss out on top five and still keep his job claims journalist Xabi Alonso must get Chelsea into the Champions League – but probably won’t get fired if he doesn’t manage it. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. It’s the international break, so there’s not a lot of Chelsea chat going around. The players are all in their national team camps, but games don’t start until tonight. That made it a good time for a general Chelsea Q and A, which is just what Bobby Vincent of Football.London has done. It’s a sign of the mood in general, on the back of a defeat to Sunderland last weekend, that questions were asked about what new manager Xabi Alonso’s target for the season were, and what it would take for him to get sacked. Alonso’s aims are clear – but he can miss them and not be sacked Xabi Alonso on the touchline. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) “Chelsea want Champions League football again with a top-four/five finish,” Vincent said. “If Xabi Alonso can’t achieve that, though, it seems unlikely he’d lose his job. Unless, of course, there was a complete capitulation. Chelsea, though, are confident they can achieve their goals this season.” Let’s all calm down and start doing what managers always say to do – take things game by game and start worrying about individual results rather than the big picture just yet. There’s a tasty run of fixtures after this break with some winnable games and some tough ones for us to test our level. In other news… Emi Martinez has given some details on the surgery he had which makes it clear his return to full health could take a while.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo at St James’ Park: A Dream Transfer or a Terrible Idea?
item.description: RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA - OCTOBER 29: Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr looks on before the Saudi Pro League match between Al Nassr and Al Kholood at Al Awwal Park on October 29, 2026 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo by Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images) | Getty Images Imagine walking into St James’ Park and seeing Cristiano Ronaldo wearing the famous black and white Newcastle United shirt. It sounds almost impossible, but could it be one of football’s most exciting transfers? Ronaldo, widely regarded as one of the greatest players ever, has achieved almost everything in the sport. However, Newcastle are an ambitious club looking to compete with Europe’s elite. Bringing the Portuguese superstar to Newcastle would certainly grab headlines, but would signing a player at this stage of his career actually benefit Newcastle? As we all know, Ronaldo coming to Newcastle would be exciting to see, and there is no doubt we would see him do exciting things with Newcastle. If Ronaldo came to Newcastle, he would bring experience, and he would be a player that you can count on like a captain. Even at this stage of his career, Ronaldo remains one of the greatest soccer players to ever walk the planet. Ronaldo would bring something to the team that other players would not; he is a very talented player who has achieved many things, winning the UEFA Champions League five times, many titles, and the Ballon d’Or five times. If Newcastle were to sign Ronaldo, they would get a lot more people to like them; they would sell millions of shirts, make more fans, and they would earn millions of dollars, and Newcastle would become an even bigger attraction. However, there are many ways the transfers would not work. Ronaldo is no longer the player he was at Man United and Real Madrid. He is now 41 years old, and he just retired from international duty, and Newcastle would need to consider his big wages and how much he would cost, because Al-Nassr is paying him millions of dollars right now; he is considered to be the richest soccer player on the planet. And would Ronaldo want to join a club that is trying to rebuild itself? Signing Ronaldo would be a crazy move and would change the soccer world because he is one of the greatest players of his time. item.title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 10
item.description: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a thrilling 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, the Dallas Cowboys return home on Sunday to host the red-hot San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys want to record their first winning streak since last November, they’ll need to bring their A-game against one of the league’s best teams. Before the two teams square off on Sunday, here are two players the Cowboys should use more in the matchup. 1) EDGE James Houston One pain point for Dallas’ defense this season has been their inability to consistently take down the opposing quarterback. While the Cowboys defense is tied for fifth in the league in pressure rate (32.8%), they have accumulated only 17 total sacks as a team, tied for the sixth-fewest. One change the Cowboys made in the past few weeks to help their struggling pass rush group was activating 27-year-old edge Jame Houston for their last three matchups. Houston, who played just 13 defensive snaps before Dallas’ Week 8 matchup against Arizona, made a big impact in his first outing with increased opportunities. In that game against the Cardinals, Houston recorded two pressures and a sack on just 11 pass-rush snaps. The former sixth-round pick had a 27.3% win percentage in that contest, the highest of any Cowboys defender, to go with a PRP of 13.6. After an impressive performance, Dallas rewarded him with more chances against the Colts. Houston played a season-high 31 defensive snaps with 18 pass-rush opportunities. While the 27-year-old couldn’t quite replicate his pass-rush success from a week prior, he recorded a 69.3 pass-rush grade on true pass sets, with a 12.5% TPS win percentage. If the Cowboys want the best chance to improve their pass rush, they need to keep increasing Houston’s usage on defense. Dallas should give Houston some of Donovan Ezeiruaku and Von Miller’s snaps to see if he can continue his upward trajectory. 2) S Alijah Clark The Cowboys defense got some unfortunate news after Sunday’s win. Safety P.J. Locke suffered a concussion and has already been ruled out for this week’s matchup against the 49ers. If the Cowboys are going to continue to play Caleb Downs primarily in the slot, Downs played 35 snaps there on Sunday; they’ll need someone to replace Locke as their second primary safety. Dallas’ coaching staff has shown an affinity for giving Markquese Bell chances when they had injuries to both starting safeties early in the year, but given how poorly Bell has performed, it’s time to give Alijah Clark the nod. Clark played 40 defensive snaps against the Eagles a few weeks back, allowing just one catch for nine yards in coverage. While Clark may not be as sure of a tackler as Bell, he is without a doubt more skilled in coverage. Dallas should give Clark the job to start alongside Malik Hooker and see if he can perform better than Bell has.

item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Carl Mays
item.description: (Original Caption) Carl Mays, New York Yankees Pitcher in action. Carl Mays probably would’ve enjoyed one single entry in the annals of baseball lore that doesn’t mention the most regrettable of the thousands of pitches that he threw across a 15-year career that saw him capture four World Series titles. Alas, even on his 135th birthday, we cannot grant that wish. No matter how great he was on the mound, his story will always be tied to that of Cleveland shortstop Ray Chapman. That’s just how it is. Carl William Mays Born: November 12, 1891 (Liberty, KY) Died: April 4, 1971 (El Cajon, CA) Yankees Tenure : 1919-23 Mays was born in Kentucky to a Methodist minister named William Mays (ah, baseball coincidences), who died when Carl was just 12 years old. The family had moved to Missouri by then, but they packed up again after William’s death, en route to Kingfisher, Oklahoma. It was a sad time for Mays’ family, but he did get the opportunity to meet his cousin, John Long. He was a catcher, and he introduced Mays to the game. Pitching to Long, Mays developed the raw skills to attract the notice of traveling teams. At the age of 20, Mays signed with the Class D Western Tri-State League’s Boise Irrigators, who offered him $90 per month. Mays was certainly worth the deal, as he pitched to a 2.08 ERA, 0.930 WHIP, and a 22-9 record in 280.2 innings. He moved up to the Class B team in Portland and again had a fine season, though won/loss record (10-15) deceived his true performance (2.45 ERA, 1.024 WHIP in 250 innings), and it was enough to get a new contract for 1914 with the Providence Grays, a Rhode Island team owned by the Detroit Tigers. The Boston Red Sox purchased the Grays from the Tigers during the season, and Mays attracted Boston’s interested with a fantastic season: 24-8 and a 2.57 ERA in 273.1 innings. Another young pitcher joined him down the stretch named Babe Ruth, and their pitching helped Providence win the pennant. By the beginning of next season, Mays was a major-league pitcher. The submariner worked mostly out of the bullpen in his rookie season, appearing in 38 games but 131.2 innings overall of 90 ERA- and 69 FIP- ball. He threw hard and was not at all afraid to throw high and inside to back hitters off the plate. Even as a rookie, he made an enemy of Ty Cobb, whose own nasty attitude clashed with Mays. On one occasion, Cobb was knocked down and then dragged a bunt up the first base line, where he spiked Mays with his sharp cleats and cut his leg. Boston and Detroit fought hard for the pennant in 1915; a 100-win season was not good enough to win the title for Detroit. Boston beat the Phillies in five games for the 1915 World Series title, but while he was a champion in his first season, Mays did not appear in any of the games. The next couple seasons saw Mays slowly transition from splitting time more evenly between the ‘pen and rotation to becoming an established rotation presence and the ace of a championship staff. item.title: UAlbany football coach says 'outside noise' hurt team in Bryant loss
item.description: UAlbany head coach Tom Perkovich during a game against Monmouth on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, at Casey Stadium in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) ALBANY - Immediately after the 31-7 loss at Bryant last Saturday, University at Albany football coach Tom Perkovich blamed himself for the Great Danes not being ready to play. Perkovich elaborated before Tuesday's practice, saying he should have done a better job cautioning his players against getting distracted by their national ranking and possible playoff hopes. "I think just continuing to talk to them about it being about us and not the outside noise a little bit more," Perkovich said. "We had talked about it day after day, but probably just needed to be a little more intentional and forthright and energetic about how I said it, maybe." With the one-sided defeat, UAlbany (6-4 overall, 4-2 league) was eliminated from Coastal Athletic Association title contention. The Great Danes dropped five spots to No. 25 in the Football Championship Subdivision coaches' poll. They remain in FCS playoff contention entering Saturday's home finale against Maine (1-8, 1-5) at Casey Stadium. However, UAlbany faces plenty of competition for one of the 13 at-large bids in the 24-team field with two weeks remaining. "People talking about playoff brackets and (there were) three games left," Perkovich said. "That's just not the time and we're an inexperienced football team, you know, in some areas and it's hard to take the human element out of it a little bit. We've just got to use it as a learning lesson and move forward." Perkovich didn't care to speculate about his team's postseason chances. He said that question would be better for UAlbany athletic director Mark Benson, who is on the FCS playoff selection committee. "What we're trying to control is what we can control, which is trying to win a game this weekend," he said. "There's always a shot of anything, but we're just trying to stay on course." Offense tries to bounce back UAlbany managed only a touchdown against Bryant after averaging 39.7 points per game during its four-game winning streak. "I just think we really couldn't get anything going," senior quarterback Kai Colon said. "I thought Bryant did a great job. They were tremendous up front and we've just got to be better at the little things. We couldn't really get any momentum going and that kind of halted us." The Great Danes offensive line struggled as the Bulldogs had five sacks and were credited with 14 quarterback hurries. It didn't help that UAlbany was forced into obvious passing downs after falling behind 28-0 in the second quarter. Perkovich said it's possible there could be changes on the offensive line against Maine. "We've got some competition going, for sure," Perkovich said. "The game we had to get into, being down four scores, is just not the game we're built for. We've got to do a better job as coaches, and obviously, players have got to execute better at times. But,

item.title: Reps threaten action against Science Minister over bill
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has threatened legislative action against the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, over his failure to attend a public hearing on a bill seeking to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund. The lawmakers warned that the ministry’s absence could delay the proposed legislation and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s efforts to attract international research grants and funding from development partners, donor agencies, United Nations organisations and Nigerians in the diaspora. The House Committee on Science and Technology expressed displeasure that neither the minister nor the ministry’s Permanent Secretary or any senior representative attended the hearing, despite the ministry’s direct responsibility for the subject matter of the bill, HB 2821. The committee also noted that the proposed legislation was sponsored by the executive and transmitted to the National Assembly by President Tinubu. Speaking at the hearing, a member of the committee, Hon. Ahmed Usman Jaha, representing Chibok, Damboa and Gwoza Federal Constituency of Borno State, described the ministry’s absence as a possible act of sabotage against the working relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government. Jaha, who spoke on behalf of the committee, said it was difficult to understand why a ministry directly concerned with an executive-sponsored bill of national importance would fail to participate in its consideration. “Unfortunately, some members of the executive are by extension sabotaging this relationship. The reason why I call it sabotage is that I see no reason whereby the executive can present a bill to the House for consideration, and that bill has national importance, but the ministry responsible for it will not show up,” he said. He disclosed that the committee had invited the Ministers of Justice, Innovation, Science and Technology, Education, Environment, Agriculture and Food Security, Health, Livestock Development, and Industry, Trade and Investment, alongside other stakeholders, to contribute to the legislative process. However, none of the invited ministers attended the hearing. Jaha said the absence of the Science and Technology Minister was particularly concerning, insisting that either the minister or the Permanent Secretary should have appeared before the committee. “We are not averse to the Ministry of Justice and other ministries that are not directly linked to the bill. But our concern this time around is the Ministry of Science and Technology. If any minister may not have time to attend, they may end up sending representatives. But the Minister of Science and Technology himself, who is more or less the sponsor of the bill, or in a worst-case scenario, the Permanent Secretary, must show up,” he said. The lawmaker further expressed concern that an international stakeholder who travelled from Kenya honoured the committee’s invitation

item.title: Singer Boj shares essential items to survive Detty December in Lagos
item.description: Nigerian singer and songwriter BOJ has shared some of his essential items for navigating the Detty December festivities, advising partygoers to prepare for the heat, crowded venues and messy environments expected during the festive season. Speaking in an interview with LSTV, the singer said the December festivities would be particularly intense, urging people to come prepared. We linked up with Nigerian singer, songwriter, and creative director Boj [ @BojDRB ] for his Detty December ESSENTIALS and he spoke facts . pic.twitter.com/tskJV12t3C — LSTVWW (@lstvww) November 12, 2026 “Everywhere is going to be hot. I don’t know if you guys have of El Nino,” he said. Listing his must-have items, BOJ identified a face towel as one of the most important things to carry, noting that the heat and activities during the festive period would make it particularly useful. “First of all, you’re going to need a face towel, very key,” he said. He also recommended wearing shoes other than white, warning that partygoers would likely encounter spilled drinks, water and crowded environments at various events. “Personally, I also think that shoes that are not white because you’re going to be stepping everywhere, you’re going to be choked of water. Just always have that because it’s going to be a lot of drinking,” he added. Detty December has become a major feature of Nigeria’s end-of-year entertainment calendar, attracting Nigerians in the diaspora and international visitors for a series of concerts, parties, festivals and social events. item.title: Read Nvidia’s internal emails about the ‘extraordinarily difficult period’ amid CEO shakeup
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia this morning, a company he co-founded in 1993. item.title: Pan-African Vibes, Epic Bar Battles, and More! Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 was an Unforgettable Experience
item.description: The 12th edition of Africa’s biggest cocktail celebration, Lagos Cocktail Week (LCW), brought its 2026 theme, “Africa Pours into Lagos,” to life in spectacular fashion, delivering an exciting fusion of Pan-African creativity, cross-border collaborations, spirited competitions, and immersive experiences that celebrated the continent’s vibrant and evolving cocktail culture. Held from October 16 to 23, 2026, the week-long festival took cocktail culture beyond borders, bringing together some of the most exciting talents and bar communities from Lagos, Accra, and Abidjan. At the heart of this year’s celebration was a powerful message: Africa’s cocktail industry thrives when creativity, culture, and expertise flow freely across borders. The celebrations took off on Sunday, October 18, as the Italian Trade Agency brought a touch of Italian sophistication to the festival with the Italian Cocktail Experience, an exclusive, invitation-only masterclass and Aperitivo Italiano held at Mr Panther, Victoria Island. The experience offered guests an opportunity to explore the artistry and traditions of Italian cocktail culture. Speaking at the event, Maurizio Ferri , Director of the Italian Trade Agency, highlighted the initiative’s goal of promoting Italian wines and spirits, featuring brands such as Campari, Aperol and Martini. The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa , founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences. The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive , the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture. One of the most exciting additions to this year’s festival was the debut of the Lagos Bar Show, a fresh take on the traditional bar hop that brought the spirit of Pan-African collaboration directly into some of Lagos’ most exciting bars. On Tuesday, October 20, Sora Lagos played host to the first guest shift, welcoming the team from Bissa, Abidjan, for an exciting collaboration featuring Dodo Plantain Infused Rum. The following evening, Wednesday, October 21, the spotlight shifted to Praia Lagos, where bartenders from Accra’s Front/Back and No. 19 Bar & Restaurant brought a taste of Ghana’s cocktail scene to Lagos, with Audry Cognac taking centre stage. The guest bartenders took over the bar, creating a selection of signature cocktails with Audry Cognac as their base. Front/Back’s bartenders served the Mantse and Ashanti, while the team from No. 19 Bar & Restaurant presented the Akwaaba, meaning “welcome,” and Nkabom, meaning “togetherness.” Praia Lagos’ bartenders also showcased their creativity with Audry Cognac, serving the Audry Passion Sour and

item.title: Zamfara commissioner dies at 50, governor mourns
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has mourned the death of the state’s Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi, who died on Wednesday at the age of 50. Shinkafi reportedly died in a hospital in Kaduna following a brief illness. In a condolence message, Lawal described his death as an irreparable loss to the state government, his family and the people of Zamfara. The governor said, “With heavy hearts and in total submission to the will of Almighty Allah (T), we received the shocking news of the passing of the Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi. “Tasiu’s death is a great loss not only to his family and the state government, but also to the people of Zamfara. “He will be remembered for his dedication, honesty, and commitment to Zamfara State.” Lawal recalled that Shinkafi had previously served as Commissioner for Youth and Sport before his redeployment to the Ministry of Commerce. Describing the deceased as a valued member of his administration and a brother in service, the governor said his contributions to governance, politics and public service would be remembered. He prayed to Almighty Allah to forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. item.title: Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list
item.description: By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Oyo State, Olusegun Agboola, has dragged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) before the Federal High Court in Abuja over the omission of his name from the commission’s list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election. Agboola alleged that unnamed political interests were behind his exclusion, describing the development as illegal, inexplicable and politically motivated. The SDP candidate, who maintained that he had fulfilled all the necessary electoral requirements, said he was seeking a court order compelling INEC to include his name on the list. In a statement on Thursday, Agboola expressed concern over what he described as the selective omission of his name despite his qualification to contest the election. He said, “The illegal and unexplainable omission of my name from the latest INEC published list as the SDP governorship candidate for Oyo State is perplexing. “Of all qualified candidates, my name was singled out and omitted from the published list without any reason from INEC.” Agboola alleged that the omission was an attempt to weaken the SDP’s political standing ahead of the election, claiming that some politicians in rival parties were uncomfortable with the party’s agenda and positions on issues affecting the state. He said, “I have been told that some people from other popular parties are behind it. They are not comfortable with all we stand for, so they want to use INEC to diminish our campaign and suppress all our efforts.” Expressing confidence in the judicial process, the candidate said he expected the court to compel INEC to correct the omission, questioning why he had to seek legal intervention after complying with the prescribed procedures. “We have followed due process and the court will soon mandate INEC to include our names, but why is that necessary?” he queried. He further alleged that his exclusion was part of a broader attempt by unnamed political interests to manipulate the electoral process and influence the outcome of the 2027 governorship election. “Some people want to use every means possible to doctor the outcome. This is sad for our democracy and shows the integrity of the umpire is damaged if this anomaly is not loudly corrected with a very public announcement from the INEC chairman,” he added. Agboola said Oyo State needed practical and sustainable solutions to unemployment, insecurity, inadequate infrastructure and other socio-economic challenges. He argued that addressing the problems required deliberate, systemic and long-term interventions rather than temporary measures. The post Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist
item.description: Armed robbers stole goods worth more than one million euros ($1.1 million) from a De Beers jewellery store in Paris Thursday before fleeing on scooters, authorities and a police source told AFP. The suspects, carrying long guns, targeted the store in the city’s 2nd arrondissement at around 11:00 am (1000 GMT). During the robbery, they brandished their weapons but did not open fire, and no one was injured, according to the Paris police. A police source estimated the value at more than one million euros, confirming an earlier report by French broadcaster Europe 1. Four suspects in balaclavas, one armed with an assault rifle, are believed to have fled on motorbikes towards the motorway, according to the same source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The Paris police said it has deployed significant resources to track down the perpetrators. The organised crime unit has opened an investigation into “armed robbery by an organised gang”, the prosecutor’s office said. Industry giant De Beers has long dominated the trade in diamonds from southern Africa. The post Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Politicians deceive voters to win elections – Kukah
item.description: The Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Matthew Kukah, has accused politicians of making unrealistic promises during election campaigns to secure votes, rather than preparing Nigerians for the realities and challenges of governance. Kukah said politicians often deploy attractive images, grand promises and appealing narratives to sell voters a vision of a better society, only to abandon their commitments after assuming office and begin offering excuses for their inability to deliver. He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at a public symposium organised by the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) in collaboration with The Kukah Centre. To illustrate the disconnect between campaign promises and governance, Kukah narrated the story of a politician who used impressive images of tarred roads, bridges, beautiful houses and children in smart school uniforms to persuade voters during his campaign. According to him, the politician won the election, but three years later, residents complained that none of the promised projects had been executed. When confronted, the politician reportedly told them: “You are confusing campaign with governance. What I did was purely a simple campaign. Governance is a difficult part.” Kukah said the response reflected a recurring pattern in Nigeria’s political system, where politicians make ambitious promises to win elections but resort to excuses after taking office. He said, “And this is why we have Nigerian politicians turn around, once they have been sworn in and after telling us all the things they want to do, and say, ‘We didn’t know that the treasury was so empty.’ Then, they start giving one excuse after the other.” The bishop argued that politicians were often more interested in creating attractive campaign narratives than communicating the realities of governance. He, however, said voters had a responsibility to interrogate political promises and assess their feasibility rather than accept campaign messages at face value. He stated, “The point I am making is that it is the business of politicians to seduce, deceive or tell us things we can’t do just to win our votes. But we are sufficiently knowledgeable, and our experience should help us to test the limits of the claims that politicians make.” Kukah urged Nigerians to develop the capacity to question politicians, scrutinise their proposals and demand accountability, stressing that citizens should not wait until elections are over before engaging the political elite. He also called for political choices that transcend ethnic, religious and class considerations. Jega urges issue-based campaigns Earlier, former Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Attahiru Jega, said the responsibility for addressing Nigeria’s electoral challenges should not rest solely on the electoral commission. item.title: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport for 30 years, eyes two others
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited. Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential. He explained that the Federal Government had been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss. According to him, the cost of maintaining airports, including personnel expenses, diesel and other operational requirements, has continued to put pressure on government finances. The minister said government lacked the resources to fully develop the non-aeronautical components of some airports, making private sector participation necessary. “Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said. He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government. He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal. The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service. He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process. “President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said. Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement. He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards. The minister also disclosed that the government had received proposals from investors interested in developing other airports, including those in Benin and Yola. He said the government was considering the proposals as part of efforts to make more airports commercially viable. item.title: Tinubu: Wike inaugurates Rivers campaign council, directs it to recruit 5 new voters daily
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has inaugurated the Presidential Campaign Council for Rivers State and directed its members to recruit at least five new voters daily to deliver votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. Wike, who performed the inauguration on Thursday, set a target of three million votes for the president in the state. He called for hard work, focus and issue-based campaigning, and dismissed recent confusion over appointments into the committees. “I am sure by Monday the list of the chairmen and members of the various sub-committees will have been prepared so that the chairmen can kick-start by inviting their various committee members. It is very important,” he said. The minister said victory in Rivers was not in doubt. “Everybody knows that we are going to win election in Rivers State. So we are not talking about winning now,” he said. Wike recalled how the three million figure came up in a discussion with Senate President Godswill Akpabio. “He said, ‘How much is the registered votes here?’ I said, ‘over three million.’ He said, ‘Okay, you will bring three million.’ I said, ‘Well, we will try’. I know that three million, if we work hard, it ia easy.” Wike urged members of the council to treat their appointments as an opportunity to work for the Rainbow Coalition, and called on them to stay united and disciplined in the face of provocation from the opposition. He cited the Olubadan and former governor of Oyo State, Oba Rasheed Ladoja who he said spoke a day earlier when the National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) paid him a courtesy visit in Oyo State. “He said if he was still in politics, if he was not a traditional ruler today, he would have joined Rainbow Coalition, that is the best way to bring every shade of opinion, members of other political parties to join hands to make sure that Mr. President is re-elected come 2027,” Wike said. Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State described the new council as bigger, wider and better coordinated than the structure that delivered victory for the president in 2023. He said former political adversaries had now closed ranks to work together for the state and the president. “Nothing is impossible. The only thing that is not possible is to revive the dead. If we take this as a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisively with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023,” Fubara said. The governor assured members who were left out that they would be accommodated in the subcommittees. He also warned against double-dealing and urged members to work with sincerity rather than profess loyalty in public while sabotaging the effort behind closed doors. “I am here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret: I have taken this position,” Fubara said. item.title: United Airlines wants you to check in, not your chatbot
item.description: United Airlines has become the latest company to slap restrictions on unauthorized third-party AI agents, warning that the bots could make unintended purchases, expose customer data, or bypass checks requiring human acknowledgment. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Amazon has also moved against unauthorized AI agents, blocking Meta's Muse (the "AI that gets it done," according to Meta's marketing) in September . The airline has yet to respond. ®

item.title: Imo East: Court orders INEC to recognise Nwole as NDC candidate
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately recognise and publish the name of Uche Nwole as the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the Imo East senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. In a judgment delivered by Justice Mohammed Umar, the court said it was satisfied that the plaintiff, Nwole, was the bona fide winner of a primary election conducted by the party, which it noted was duly monitored by INEC. It held that, in view of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the NDC ought to have nominated and forwarded the plaintiff’s name to the electoral body as its senatorial candidate. According to the court, the NDC could not lawfully nominate a consensus candidate other than the one who emerged from its INEC-monitored primary election. Consequently, aside from issuing an order of perpetual injunction restraining the party from nominating or submitting any other name for the election, the court barred INEC from accepting, listing or publishing any purported NDC candidate who allegedly emerged from a primary election that was never held or monitored by the commission, or any purported consensus candidate whose nomination breached Sections 87(1) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026. The judgment followed suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/1225/2026, in which the NDC, INEC and Hon. Onyeagucha Uchechukwu were the 1st to 3rd defendants. The plaintiff alleged that although he secured the highest number of valid votes cast in the primary election, the party sidelined him and chose the 3rd defendant as its flag bearer for the senatorial poll. Justice Umar said that, after careful examination of all the evidence adduced in the matter, he was satisfied that the plaintiff’s case deserved to succeed. He therefore granted all seven principal reliefs the plaintiff sought. Among other things, the court held: “A declaration is made that, upon the construction of the clear, unambiguous and express provisions, spirit and tenor of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the 1st Defendant duly conducted primary elections, which were duly monitored by the 2nd Defendant, for all aspirants seeking to be nominated as the candidate of the party to contest the elective position of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “A declaration is made that, upon a careful construction and interpretation of Section 87(1), (2) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026, the 1st Defendant, having conducted a primary election in accordance with Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act, cannot lawfully nominate a consensus candidate to contest the office of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “A declaration is made that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), being a body established by law, must at all times obey its constitution; respect, observe and implem

item.title: Nigeria’s exports to China rise 81% to $2.25bn
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria’s exports to China rose by 81 per cent to $2.25 billion in the first half of 2026, while bilateral trade between both countries increased by 35 per cent to $17.4 billion, the Chinese Embassy has said. The Cultural Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and Director of the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria, Mr Yang Jiaxing, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 launch ceremony of the Voice of Nigeria (VON) China-Nigeria Bridge Programme. Yang attributed the growth to expanding economic cooperation between the two countries, saying China’s zero-tariff policy for 53 African countries, including Nigeria, which took effect in May 2026, would create more opportunities for Nigerian exports. He said China’s trade with African countries reached $207.4 billion in the first half of 2026, while imports from the continent rose to $28.5 billion between May and June. According to him, imports from Nigeria recorded year-on-year growth of more than 40 per cent in both May and June, reflecting stronger trade relations between the two countries. He said: “In the first half of this year, bilateral trade between China and Nigeria reached $17.4 billion, up 35 per cent year-on-year. China’s imports from Nigeria amounted to $2.25 billion, representing a remarkable increase of 81 per cent.” Yang described the China-Nigeria Bridge Programme as a platform for promoting cultural understanding, media cooperation and closer relations between citizens of both countries. The programme, jointly initiated by the Chinese Embassy, the Africa Regional Bureau of Xinhua News Agency and VON, provides Mandarin lessons and reports on China-Africa relations. Also speaking, the Director-General of VON, Jibrin Baba Ndace, said the introduction of Mandarin as the organisation’s ninth broadcast language would strengthen Nigeria’s international presence and enable it to communicate its stories to a wider audience. Ndace, who was represented by the Director of General Services, Alhaji Danladi Abubakar, said the service would promote Nigeria’s culture, tourism, business opportunities and national image among Chinese-speaking audiences. He said the initiative followed agreements reached between Nigeria and China at the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation held in Beijing. According to him, VON also signed agreements with Xinhua News Agency and the Chinese Embassy in 2026 to promote content sharing, staff training, broadcasting capacity and media cooperation. In his remarks, the Executive Secretary of the Nigeria Press Council, Dili Ezughah, described the programme as an important step towards strengthening cultural diplomacy and people-to-people relations. He urged the partners to sustain the initiative, saying its success should be measured by its ability to promote mutual understanding and lasting relationships between citizens of both countries. item.title: Ododo flags off 38.5km Kogi road project
item.description: …Promises to End Decades of Poor Access By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, on Thursday flagged off the construction of the 38.5-kilometre Kabba–Olle-Bunu–Iluke-Bunu Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area, promising to address decades of poor road infrastructure in the area. The project, flagged off at Oke-Ofin, is expected to improve connectivity among communities in Bunu land, ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand access to economic opportunities. Speaking at the ceremony, Ododo described the project as the fulfilment of a long-standing aspiration of the people, assuring residents that his administration would not abandon any community, irrespective of its location. He said the road would mark a new chapter for the area by reconnecting communities that had remained isolated for years. The governor recalled how the deplorable condition of the road had affected farmers, businesses and residents, explaining that farmers struggled to transport their produce to markets, while indigenes living outside the state found it difficult to visit their ancestral homes. He disclosed that his personal experience during a visit to Iluke-Bunu following a security incident involving students had strengthened his resolve to rehabilitate the road. Ododo said the project was part of his administration’s commitment to complementing efforts to restore security with tangible development, stressing that peace without infrastructure and economic opportunities would remain incomplete. According to him, the road would facilitate the transportation of yams, cassava, cashew and other agricultural produce, reduce transportation costs, shorten travel time and stimulate commercial activities across Bunu land. The governor acknowledged the support of President Bola Tinubu, saying the increased financial resources available to state governments following the Federal Government’s economic reforms had helped subnational governments execute major infrastructure projects. He urged residents to embrace unity and take ownership of the project by monitoring its execution, protecting construction equipment and ensuring that quality standards were maintained. The Commissioner for Information and Communications, Kingsley Femi Fanwo, described the flag-off as a historic moment, citing his personal connection to Bunu land. Fanwo recalled trekking from Iluke to Ole-Bunu because of the poor condition of the road, which he said had remained in a deplorable state for more than 35 years. He said the project would open up several communities in Bunu to greater economic and social opportunities, adding that future generations would remember the intervention. The Commissioner for Education, an indigene of the benefiting community, also thanked the governor, describing the project as a major development for residents who had endured years of hardship because of the inaccessible road. On one side, the US is defending dollar supremacy with stablecoins. On the other, China and Russia are rolling out state-controlled digital currencies like the digital yuan and digital ruble. item.title: 194 make first class as UNIZIK graduates 16,842
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Nnamdi Azikiwe University (UNIZIK), Awka, Anambra State, will graduate 16,842 students at its 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies scheduled for November 15 to 20, 2026, with 194 of the graduands earning First Class honours. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Anyaehie, disclosed this during a pre-convocation press briefing in Awka, where he also highlighted the institution’s academic, administrative, technological and infrastructural achievements. Anyaehie said the graduands comprised 14,803 first-degree recipients and 2,039 postgraduate students from the 2025 and 2026 academic sessions. A breakdown of the results showed that 4,230 students obtained Second Class Upper Division, while 7,992 graduated with Second Class Lower Division. Another 1,936 students obtained Third Class honours, while 65 graduated with Pass degrees. A further 486 earned unclassified medical and professional degrees. At the postgraduate level, 603 candidates obtained Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees, 29 earned Master of Philosophy/PhD degrees, 1,113 obtained Master’s degrees, while 294 graduated with Postgraduate Diplomas (PGDs). The Vice-Chancellor described the forthcoming convocation as an opportunity to celebrate the university’s growth and showcase achievements recorded under his administration’s vision of making a greater UNIZIK possible. He said the university had been ranked joint fourth among Nigerian universities in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings. He also disclosed that UNIZIK’s debate team won the 13th All Nigerian Universities Debate Championship (ANUDC), marking the first time the institution had clinched the title. Anyaehie recalled that the university’s athletes also won silver and bronze medals at the 12th Federation of African University Sports (FASU) Games held in Cairo, Egypt. On digital infrastructure, he said the university had been selected for the Federal Government’s $617.7 million Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) programme, supported by the Bank of Industry, Agence Française de Développement and the African Development Bank/Islamic Development Bank. He said the institution had expanded its internet bandwidth to 2Gbps through the Agence Française de Développement-Nigeria Research and Education Network (AFD-NgREN), adding that equipment supplied by Galaxy Backbone had been installed to activate an additional 300Mbps. The Vice-Chancellor further disclosed that his administration had established a TETFund ICT Experience Centre at Hall 2 of the university’s Digital Library to support training and research in artificial intelligence, robotics, cybersecurity and software engineering. item.title: Oyo targets $3.4trn African market for artisans, creative businesses
item.description: By Adeola Badru Oyo State Government has unveiled plans to position local artisans, creative entrepreneurs and small businesses to tap into the estimated $3.4 trillion African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) market and expand their access to global export opportunities. The state government said it was determined to transform its rich cultural heritage into a commercially viable creative industry capable of generating wealth, creating employment and attracting foreign exchange through exports. Governor Seyi Makinde stated this at the Investment and Export Promotion for Art and Craft Businesses in Oyo State, tagged Oyo State Business Forum 2026: Where Oyo’s Makers Meet the World’s Buyers. The forum, held at the Ministry of Local Government Hall, Secretariat, Ibadan, was organised by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment Promotion Agency (OYSIPA). Represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Musibau Babatunde, the governor said the initiative was a deliberate effort to reposition Oyo State as a major destination for creative enterprise and investment. Addressing government officials, investors, development partners, captains of industry and entrepreneurs, Makinde said the state was determined to ensure that locally produced goods gained international recognition and commercial value. “Today, we are not just gathered for another forum. We are gathered to make a declaration that Oyo State will no longer be known for its history, but for its entrepreneurial spirit. “We are gathered here around a common ambition to transform what our people create with their hands into products that the world recognises, values and buys,” he said. Tracing Oyo’s commercial heritage to the old Oyo Empire, Babatunde noted that the state had historically played an important role in regional commerce, with its people trading textiles, beads, ironworks and other products across West Africa long before the emergence of modern international trade. He said AfCFTA had presented another significant opportunity for the state to reclaim its position as a commercial powerhouse by expanding the reach of locally manufactured and processed products. According to him, the continental trade agreement is creating a single African market of approximately 1.4 billion people, with a combined economic output of about $3.4 trillion. He, however, challenged the state to move beyond recognising the opportunities offered by the agreement and take concrete steps to secure a significant share of its benefits. “The question before us is simple. Will Oyo State merely absorb this opportunity, or will we position ourselves to benefit from it? My answer is clear. Oyo State will be an active participant, and our artisans, creative entrepreneurs and small businesses will be among the driving forces of this ambition,” he said. The SSG further claimed that Oyo State was the first sub-national government in Africa to key into the AfCFTA framewo

item.title: BNY Mellon Raises Its Strive (ASST) Stake 28% to $7 Million as Monday’s 13F Deadline Nears
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BNY Mellon Raises Its Strive (ASST) Stake 28% to $7 Million as Monday’s 13F Deadline Nears Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) raised its stake in Strive (ASST) by 28% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 5 shows, lifting the position to 237,100 shares worth $6.97 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 51,544 shares from the 185,556 BNY reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $2.02 million. Most of the dollar jump is the stock. ASST’s implied price on the two filings rose from $10.91 at June 30 to $29.41 at Sept. 30, so the disclosed stake more than tripled in value even though the share count rose 28%. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. BNY filed a combination report that folds in holdings across its group, so the Strive line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. The bank oversees $63.4 trillion in assets under custody and/or administration and $2.2 trillion in assets under management, both as of Sept. 30. The Strive position is still modest next to other bitcoin-linked lines on the same report. BNY held 1,056,230 shares of Strategy (MSTR) worth $161.7 million and 162,072 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $7.67 million, a stake that nearly doubled from 85,282 shares at June 30 and is now about the same size as the Strive line. Monday’s deadline still has a few large filers outstanding Institutional managers that exercise investment discretion over $100 million or more in 13F securities have 45 days after quarter-end to disclose those holdings. That window ran to Nov. 14, a Saturday, so the deadline is Monday, Nov. 16. JPMorgan Chase filed its third-quarter 13F on Thursday. Wells Fargo, Millennium Management and Schonfeld Strategic Advisors had not appeared on the SEC’s EDGAR system as of Thursday morning. Those remaining names are among the larger managers whose bitcoin ETF and treasury-stock lines, if they report any, are not yet on the public record. BNY was earlier than most. It filed on Nov. 5, more than a week before the deadline, which is why the Strive line is already public while a handful of large managers are still unaccounted for. Other banks already disclosed bitcoin ETF positions Barclays, in a 13F filed Nov. 6, reported 3,942,900 IBIT shares worth $186.7 million at Sept. 30, up 48% from 2,658,147 shares three months earlier. Citigroup, in a filing dated Nov. 4, reported 521,144 IBIT shares worth $24.7 million, up from 347,114 at June 30, and a new $118.9 million position in Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC), or 1,636,387 shares, that did not appear on its June 30 filing. Those lines carry the same caveat as BNY’s Strive stake: a 13F gathers client, managed and trading-book positions, not proof a bank put its own capital into bitcoin or into a bitcoin treasury stock.
