item.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
item.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. The Vespera 3 also has CovalENS, Vaonis’s mosaic imaging system, which captures adjacent sections of sky to produce a larger image. That’s helpful for obj

item.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
item.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

item.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
item.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. item.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
item.description: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

item.title: Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Rumble’s AI pivot takes over The bitcoin drawdown came in a quarter dominated by Quake AI, the cloud and AI infrastructure unit Rumble built around Northern Data, the German GPU operator it acquired in June. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Executives said on the call that about $39 million of that came from writing up the value of Northern Data’s assets in purchase accounting. “Quake AI is now the engine of our business,” CEO Chris Pavlovski said. “We have real assets running real AI workloads for real customers and generating real cash.” The video business itself grew more slowly. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. Cash has been falling as well. RUM Group ended September with $134.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $203.3 million at the end of June and $237.9 million at the end of 2025. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

item.title: BlackRock’s IBIT Bleeds $2 Billion in Nine Straight Days of Outflows
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock’s IBIT Bleeds $2 Billion in Nine Straight Days of Outflows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost another $269.7 million on Wednesday, its ninth straight session of redemptions, as U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a fifth consecutive day of net outflows totaling $299.8 million. Across the nine sessions since Oct. 30, IBIT has shed about $2 billion. The fund, the largest of the U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, has seen money leave on every trading day so far in November. The broader group has fared only slightly better. The 11 funds have lost about $1.44 billion over the past five trading days and roughly $1.88 billion in November, with outflows on seven of the month’s eight sessions. The lone exception was Nov. 4, when $74.6 million came in, even as IBIT itself bled $201.2 million that day. IBIT accounts for about $1.77 billion of November’s outflows, or roughly 94% of the total. Wednesday’s selling was concentrated. Besides IBIT, Grayscale’s GBTC lost $39.1 million, while Morgan Stanley’s MSBT was the only fund to take in money, about $9 million. The rest of the funds reported no flows. IBIT streak still short of this year’s worst The current run is not a record. Both the group and IBIT went 13 straight trading days without an inflow from May 15 to June 3, the longest outflow streaks of 2026. IBIT followed that with an 11-session streak from June 17 to July 2. Still, the size of the recent withdrawals stands out. IBIT’s two largest daily outflows of the year both came this month: $405.3 million on Nov. 2 and $403 million on Nov. 6. The selling has also flipped the year. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs are now down about $1.42 billion in net flows for 2026, compared with roughly $25.2 billion of inflows at the same point last year. The Australian Financial Review noted Thursday that the selling has erased this year’s net inflows into the funds. IBIT is still positive for the year, with about $2.45 billion in net inflows in 2026 and roughly $64.5 billion since it launched in January 2024. That cushion has shrunk quickly. IBIT took in about $932 million in October, and November’s withdrawals have already erased that amount nearly twice over. The withdrawals come just days after BlackRock argued that security fears were driving bitcoin whales out of self-custody and into IBIT. Why bitcoin ETF investors are pulling back The outflows began before this week’s worst headlines but have picked up alongside them. A hotter-than-expected October inflation report on Tuesday lifted bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and Polymarket odds of a hike climbed to about 97%, Yahoo Finance reported . Higher rates make cash and bonds more attractive relative to assets like bitcoin. Tech stocks have added pressure. Nvidia shares fell roughly 9% after Wednesday’s close following reports that its board was preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, and Nasdaq 100 futures slid with them. item.title: Bitcoin Price Falls Below $72,000 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down and Strategy (MSTR) Slides
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls Below $72,000 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down and Strategy (MSTR) Slides Bitcoin price fell below $72,000 on Thursday morning, its lowest level since mid-August, after Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang had resigned and Strategy shares slid following MSCI’s confirmation of an index exit, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The selling started after Wednesday’s close. Bitcoin slipped from about $74,700 to near $73,400 by 6 p.m. ET, then drifted sideways overnight. A second leg lower began around 6 a.m., and the bitcoin price briefly dipped to about $72,200 shortly after 8 a.m. The decline accelerated later in the morning, and bitcoin traded as low as about $71,670 around 9:29 a.m. That move pushed the bitcoin price below the low near $72,700 it set after Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected inflation report . It now trades roughly $31,200 below where it stood one year ago. Nvidia CEO steps down, and the bitcoin price follows Nvidia (NVDA) said Thursday that Huang has resigned as president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately. The company named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first board chair. Kress will continue as chief financial officer while she serves in the interim role. The board is searching for a permanent successor and said it will consider internal and external candidates. Nvidia is still scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter results on Nov. 17. The resignation follows reports of extramarital relationships, including one that has raised national security concerns in Washington. Sen. Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, had told CNBC that Huang should step down, saying he was “so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail.” Nvidia shares fell about 13% at Thursday’s open. Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.4% and S&P 500 futures fell about 0.7%, while Dow futures were nearly flat. Intel, Marvell Technology and Micron were down between about 5% and 7.5%, and CoreWeave dropped about 16%, giving back most of Wednesday’s 24.7% surge. Data center firms IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific also traded lower. Bitcoin price has moved with tech for most of this month. It fell on Monday when an earlier Nvidia probe rattled markets, then lagged Wednesday’s rebound in chip stocks. Thursday’s slide wiped out that small gain and then some. Strategy slides after MSCI confirms index exit Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, fell about 7% at the open after MSCI confirmed it will remove the stock from its indexes. MSCI’s November review removed Strategy from the MSCI USA Index , a step that also takes it out of the MSCI World and ACWI indexes, effective at the Nov. 30 close. Japan’s Metaplanet is also slated for removal. Index funds will sell MSTR shares, not bitcoin, and nothing in the rules requires Strategy to sell its coins. item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
item.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationhip another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. A two-week downfall News of the scandal first broke barely a couple of weeks ago, on October 29, when claims surfaced that Huang had been the target of an espionage plot involving a Chinese businesswoman working for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed which was a customer of Nvidia. According to the New York Times , US intelligence had reason to believe the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to gather information about Nvidia and its operations for the Beijing government. Megaspeed also faces claims it was illicitly shipping Nvidia products to China, in violation of US export controls. Any relationship between Huang and a Chinese operative would be enormously concerning, as the US has been trying to keep advanced technology for AI out of the hands of the country, allegedly for security reasons, fearing it might be used for military purposes. For its part, Beijing rejects the spying allegations, saying they are part of a smear campaign against China. Shortly after Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating Huang, he sent an email to Nvidia staff apologizing and confessing to having an affair, though he did not explicitly name Alice Huang in his public apology. It seemed like the leather-jacketed leader might just hang on, since it was difficult to imagine anyone other than him leading the company after all this time. But Nvidia’s shares fell 4.3 percent on November 9 and a further 5.5 percent the following day, wiping around $430 billion off its market value, amid all the speculation. Then the claim emerged regarding a second affair, with an employee at Nvidia who reported to him, and many commentators took it as a sign the game was up. Huang resigned the same day the news broke. He made the declaration as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, inaugurated members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in the State. He urged members to demonstrate through their actions that they are committed to the political cause ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said he expected members to be honest about their political convictions, stressing that those unwilling to support his position should openly take a different path rather than engage in double-dealing. He said his political decision is firm and would not be different whether expressed publicly or privately. “Don’t say you’re openly with me, and behind you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret. I have taken this position, and anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way.” Gov. Fubara also urged members to put past political differences behind them, noting that the new campaign council has brought together a broader spectrum of political stakeholders, including some who were previously in opposition. He described the expanded composition of the council as an advantage that could strengthen the coalition’s chances if members worked together. Recalling the 2023 general elections, the governor said a similar political structure had helped secure victory for him and President Bola Tinubu, expressing confidence that the new council could deliver even more votes in 2027. He challenged members to approach the assignment with determination, insisting that electoral success would depend on their willingness to work collectively towards a common objective. “If we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisive, with a stronger vote that is more than what we did in 2023.” The governor congratulated members of the inaugurated council and assured those who were not included in the initial list that additional committees would be constituted and the structure could still be expanded. He expressed appreciation to the council’s leadership and other political stakeholders for their efforts, praying for success in the task ahead. item.title: Huang powers and bankrolls AI revolution: Nvidia CEO caught between 'a rock and a very hard place'
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of France's Institute of Digital Sovereignty. Benhamou examines the intersection of traditional espionage, geopolitical rivalry and the extraordinary concentration of power within the global AI industry. Discussing allegations surrounding Nvidia's leadership, he describes the chipmaker as "the banker of the global AI system," a striking characterization that captures the company's importance not merely as a semiconductor manufacturer, but as a central actor in the economic and technological infrastructure underpinning the AI boom. "Because humans stay humans." Benhamou identifies one of the central paradoxes of the artificial intelligence revolution: even as technological systems acquire unprecedented strategic and economic importance, the individuals who control them remain susceptible to familiar forms of influence, manipulation and misjudgment.

item.title: ‘To them, we’re just NPCs’: the artists and activists challenging Trump’s video game propaganda
item.description: Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. After an explosion of news coverage, Arcade caught the attention of the games industry. The Tetris Company warned on social media that it “took copyright infringement very seriously.” Days later, the game was removed from the White House site. However, aside from a March 2026 statement from the Pokémon Company condemning the White House for using its characters in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) propaganda, major video game companies have been relatively silent in the face of the administration’s widespread usage of their IP. item.title: Vast data dump from Euclid space telescope reveals stunning galaxies
item.description: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The European Space Agency has just released a vast batch of observations of the sky captured by the Euclid space telescope. Launched in 2023, the telescope is currently on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to build the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos ever created . The latest observations – catchily titled DR1-Foundation – cover an area of the sky as big as 9500 full moons. The collection includes 900 million galaxies. The mosaic of 740 images at the top of the article, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, covers 367 square degrees of the northern sky. At full resolution, this snapshot runs to 500 gigapixels. Advertisement The bright oval in the lower left portion of the patchwork image is the spiral galaxy Messier 81, which is some 12 million light years from Earth. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Messier 81 in greater detail, along with part of the M81 group of galaxies that also bears its name – an honour bestowed on it as the largest galaxy of the bunch. To the lower left is the smaller galaxy NGC 3077, and the patches of wispy blue cloud throughout the images are galactic cirrus, which are actually in the foreground and part of our own home galaxy. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO Here, Messier 81 is shown in even greater detail, in an image taken at the full resolution available to Euclid. The haze dominating the right side of the frame is the disc of Messier 81, inside which individual stars are visible. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO This hazy galaxy is NGC 1291, around 33 million light years away. The image was made from two taken by Euclid and then cropped. In the background, even more distant galaxies are visible – the furthest away of which show up in red. Stars are still actively forming within NGC 1291, and can be seen as small blue-hued dots. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies lying around 800 million light years away. The cluster is home to a diverse array of galaxies, including whirling spirals and fuzzy ellipticals. In the centre of the image is a strong gravitational lens, where the light travelling to us from a more distant galaxy has been warped by a massive object in the foreground.

item.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
item.description: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Here are some of the best places to watch the moon's shadow cross what was once the Roman Empire. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Baelo Claudia, Spain Baelo Claudia's Roman ruins overlook Bolonia beach and the Strait of Gibraltar. (Image credit: Andrea Pucci via Getty Images) Location: near Tarifa, Andalucía, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:44 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 31 seconds Historical cloud cover: 12% Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east Roman ruins, an Atlantic beach and the mountains of Africa could all share the frame with the eclipsed sun at Baelo Claudia. Founded in the second century B.C., this remarkably well-preserved Roman city near Bolonia beach includes a forum, basilica, theater, temples, baths and a decumanus maximus (east-west street), all set against forested hills and a vast coastal sand dune. For photographers, the possibilities are exceptional — columns and temples may provide an ancient foreground, while wider compositions could incorporate the beach and dunes. On particularly clear days, Morocco is visible across the Strait of Gibraltar — potentially putting Roman ruins, two continents and a total solar eclipse into one extraordinary scene. 2. Málaga Roman Theatre, Spain The Roman Theatre at the foot of the Málaga Alcazaba dates back to the 1st century BC. (Image credit: Manfred Gottschalk via Getty Images) Location: Málaga, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 1 minute, 57 seconds Historical cloud cover: 9% Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east Few eclipse locations can offer two civilizations in the same photograph. Málaga's Roman Theatre was built in the first century B.C., when the city was part of the Roman province of Hispania, and today sits directly beneath the Alcazaba, the imposing Muslim-era palace-fortress that dominates the hillside above. item.title: US Does Not ‘Need A Deal With Iran’, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he was directing Vice President JD Vance to focus solely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations with Tehran. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. The development was after the US President defended the war against Iran Wednesday at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defense secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum. “The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington. “When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer.” U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP The war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 US service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979.” U.S. President Donald Trump and U.S. Vice President JD Vance participate in a wreath-laying ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2025 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP He stressed that US forces were acting to halt Iran’s capacity to build a nuclear weapon. Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America’s lost service members. During his speech before troops, veterans and top officials in his administration, Trump namechecked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was in attendance, saying he had “done a fantastic job.” Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort — launched by an outgoing Republican lawmaker — to impeach Hegseth for allegedly waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. Hegseth stirred even more controversy at the ceremony: an Army sentinel watching over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded a small group of people that included Hegseth, his wife and several aides, when some of them laughed after posing for a picture in front of the sacred site. “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” the sentinel called out,

item.title: Quantum leap: IBM plans to scale beyond 1,000 qubits in 2027 with Nighthawk r3 processor
item.description: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction. item.description: Explore Hubble Hubble Home Overview About Hubble The History of Hubble Hubble Timeline Why Have a Telescope in Space? Hubble by the Numbers At the Museum FAQs Impact & Benefits Hubble’s Impact & Benefits Science Impacts Cultural Impact Technology Benefits Impact on Human Spaceflight Astro Community Impacts Science Hubble Science Science Themes Science Highlights Science Behind Discoveries Universe Uncovered Hubble’s Partners in Science Hubble & Citizen Science SI & Hubble Science Explore the Night Sky Observatory Hubble Observatory Hubble Design Mission Operations Science Operations Astronaut Missions to Hubble Hubble vs. Webb Hubble vs. Roman Team Hubble Team Career Aspirations Hubble Astronauts Multimedia Images Videos Online Activities e-Books Sonifications Podcasts 3D Hubble Models Lithographs Fact Sheets Posters Hubble on the NASA App Glossary News Hubble News Social Media Media Resources 35th Anniversary More Online Activities 5 min read NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman A collage of strong gravitational lenses observed by Hubble, some of which will be followed up by observations with the Roman Space Telescope, which launched in August 2026. Lenses like these will be used to investigate the evolution of galaxies and dark matter. Credit: NASA, ESA, and X. Huang (University of San Francisco); Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Gravitational lensing, first predicted by Albert Einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. The effect is similar to that of a giant lens in space that allows astronomers to view objects much farther away than any telescope could see on its own. The lenses in this image formed from the precise alignment of a distant background galaxy with the mass of a foreground galaxy, creating distorted and magnified images of the background galaxy that appear as arcs around the foreground galaxy. Astronomers will use these observations of a large and varied population of gravitational lenses to construct lens models that will help determine how much mass is in the lensing system’s foreground galaxy – and potentially prove or dispel a theory about dark matter. Astronomers study the amount of distortion of the lensed background galaxies to determine the quantity and distribution of mass in the foreground galaxy, including its invisible dark matter. Hubble views the cosmos primarily in visible and ultraviolet light with some infrared coverage, providing a comprehensive, high-resolution view of individual objects. The event, which was originally set for 7 December, will bring together leading African footballers, coaches and teams at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts in Iganmu. Spanning 18 award categories across men’s and women’s football, the 2026 CAF Awards will celebrate the finest players, coaches, national teams, and clubs across the continent while bringing football royalty, Nollywood stars, Afrobeats performers, and fashion insiders together on one red carpet. The 2026 shortlists come with a notable twist for the host nation. item.title: Hackers exploiting ScreenConnect plugin flaw to spread malware across hundreds of PCs
item.description: Hackers have used a dodgy third-party ScreenConnect extension to push malware onto at least 288 machines across 48 organizations, prompting ConnectWise to disable a handful of plugins in hundreds of customer environments. Security outfit Huntress first raised the alarm in a Reddit post on Wednesday, warning of an active campaign targeting cloud-hosted ScreenConnect instances. At the time, its security operations center was tracking six compromised managed service providers (MSPs) and more than 286 affected endpoints, with the numbers still climbing. ConnectWise acquired popular remote supporttool ScreenConnect in February, 2015. Huntress spotted the attacks at around 1747 UTC, when someone began using ScreenConnect's remote command feature to install rogue clients on machines managed by multiple IT service providers. All 288 endpoints were hit within 90 minutes, with roughly a third compromised in the first ten minutes. Huntress suspects more MSPs may have been compromised, as the attackers appeared to be numbering their victims sequentially, with the numbers suggesting earlier attacks that it hadn't detected. The attackers deployed a 16-file malware toolkit dubbed SCKit, which installs a separate ScreenConnect client to maintain remote access even if the legitimate connection is shut down. It also contains code designed to spread the infection to IT technicians and potentially other customers under their control. Huntress has since traced the activity to a possible authentication weakness in RMM+, a third-party extension that lets other management tools issue commands through ScreenConnect without technicians using its console. Versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 of the extension contain a flaw that means installations without a configured access key will accept a blank one. Because RMM+ operates independently of ScreenConnect's normal user accounts and authentication controls, an attacker could potentially execute commands without defeating MFA. Huntress said the findings matched what its investigators saw during the attacks, with commands reaching machines across several ScreenConnect installations despite no corresponding login activity. The researchers also confirmed that the attacks affected ScreenConnect versions 26.6.6.9747 and 26.7.6.9783, meaning administrators running the latest releases weren't necessarily safe. ConnectWise has acknowledged that third-party extensions may have been involved but has stopped short of confirming how the attackers initially gained access. In a security advisory , the company said it was investigating unauthorized access to certain partner environments and had identified approximately 400 installations containing at least one extension from the RMM+ family. It has disabled five extensions, including RMM+, RMM Plus, and Labtech Plus, wherever it can do so remotely, and urged customers running their own ScreenConnect servers to follow suit. item.title: Through NASA’s Lens: Capturing Space Shuttle Endeavour’s Move to LA
item.description: 3 Min Read Through NASA’s Lens: Capturing Space Shuttle Endeavour’s Move to LA A spectacular sight as NASA’s Shuttle Carrier Aircraft with space shuttle Endeavour atop soars over the Golden Gate Bridge. Credits: NASA/Carla Thomas As a new exhibit opens showcasing NASA’s space shuttle Endeavour, NASA photographers look back at the final mission. These photographers documented the iconic images shared around the world on Sept. 21, 2012, while millions watched space shuttle Endeavour fly on top of the agency’s 747 Shuttle Carrier Aircraft for the last time. Endeavour’s new home at the California Science Center in Los Angeles will reopen the weekend of Nov. 13, displayed upright in launch position, ready to inspire the next generation of space explorers. NASA/Lori Losey “Chasing Endeavour’s final ferry flight over Southern California was, without a doubt, a leading highlight of my 37-year career at NASA,” said Lori Losey, lead videographer at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. “I advocated for two chase aircraft to be used in the LA area so we could dedicate one aircraft to photo and one to video. It was this beautiful dance of alternating altitudes and swapping positions between landmarks to maximize both of us capturing the legendary imagery.” Two photographers and one videographer, all based at NASA Armstrong, had a leading hand in preparing the Endeavour’s flight to Los Angeles, and in deciding where else the aircraft would fly around California on its final journey. Agency pilots planned the route to fly across some of California’s most iconic landmarks and the imagery team strategized about how to best capture the images. Thousands of visitors to Disneyland and Disney’s California Adventure parks got a special treat when NASA’s Shuttle Carrier Aircraft with space shuttle Endeavour on top flew over at low level during its flyover of Los Angeles. NASA/Jim Ross “The most fun thing about this project was seeing the excitement of the people on the ground as we flew over the different landmarks,” said Jim Ross, NASA Armstrong’s lead photographer. “People in the Los Angeles area really came out and supported the Endeavour flyover. We saw so many supporters at Griffith Park and Disneyland.” Photographer Carla Thomas said seeing the standing-room-only crowd below the California State Capitol in Sacramento filled her with pride. After joining the agency in the wake of the Challenger tragedy, she reflected on the opportunity to document NASA’s return to flight. The space shuttle Endeavour and its 747 carrier aircraft makes a low-level flyover of the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. NASA/Jim Ross Endeavour was escorted by NASA Armstrong’s F/A-18s and an F-15, which carried the photo and video teams in the back seats. item.title: Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars
item.description: null Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist! The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Big Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen. There is just 18,100 light-years, or roughly one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way, between the supermassive black holes, which have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million times that of the sun. That makes Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua the most compact quasar pair found during a period of the universe's history known as Cosmic Dawn , shortly after the birth of the first stars, galaxies, and black holes. "There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our universe, much less two," research team leader Silvia Onorato of the NOIRLab said in a statement . "We observed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the universe was only a thirteenth of its age and, astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today." How were supermassive black holes over fed at Cosmic Dawn Quasars occur when the supermassive black holes that sit at the heart of large galaxies are surrounded by a flattened cloud of swirling gas and dust called an "accretion disk," from which they feed or "accrete" matter. The immense gravity of the central black hole causes friction, heating the accretion disk and causing it to glow, often brighter than the combined light of every star in the surrounding galaxy. We see that glow as a quasar. Finding such objects in the recent cosmic history of the 13.8-billion-year-old universe isn't troubling, though finding compact pairs of them is still extremely rare. Such pairs should be common because the merger of galaxies that brings together supermassive black holes is frequent. That should lead to an abundance of pairs of quasars with a separation less than the typical size of a galaxy. There are three reasons this has proven tricky. Firstly, the "quasar phase" of a supermassive black hole is relatively short on cosmic terms. Secondly, even relatively close quasar pairs are very far away, making them faint and hard to detect with ground-based telescopes. Finally, at such great distances and with such a small separation between the two supermassive black holes, the individual members of a quasar pair are hard to individually resolve. Yet, astronomers do find quasar pairs. Sometimes at distances and times that they would probably ra

item.title: Suspected Thugs Attack NDC Supporters In Lagos Ahead Of Peter Obi’s Town Hall
item.description: Suspected political thugs on Thursday, November 12, 2026, attacked members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Oregun area of Ikeja, Lagos State, disrupting preparations for a town hall meeting scheduled to be addressed by the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The incident, which occurred around 11:00 a.m. at the Classique Event Centre along Kudirat Abiola Way, sent scores of attendees scampering for safety and triggered panic in the surrounding commercial district. Motorists plying Kudirat Abiola Way were forced to make abrupt U-turns to avoid the melee, while pedestrians fled the area. Crowd of NDC supporters gather outside town hall after attack by thugs. According to witnesses at the scene, neither Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, nor Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, had arrived at the venue when the attackers struck. Shattered glass on the floor, as captured by our reporter at the scene of the disrupted town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Oregun, Lagos State, on Thursday, November 12, 2026 : Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV https://t.co/lR2QKFNf8v — Channels Television (@channelstv) November 12, 2026 Shattered glass littered the floor of the disrupted venue, while several vehicles belonging to NDC members and supporters stood vandalised within the premises. One party supporter, speaking to Channels Television after sustaining a head injury, alleged that hoodlums armed with cutlasses invaded the area in an attempt to derail the gathering. He noted that additional NDC members were mobilised to resist the assailants, eventually forcing them to retreat. “When I arrived out here, we reacted to our president without fear. They started fighting back, breaking our vehicles, and destroying property,” the injured supporter told Channels Television, adding that attendees retaliated in self-defence despite being outnumbered and warning of heightened tensions ahead of the 2027 elections. ﻿ Armed policemen and security patrol vehicles were subsequently deployed to the Classique Event Centre to restore order and prevent further escalation. Following the arrival of law enforcement, the atmosphere gradually stabilised, with NDC supporters seen dancing, singing, and defiantly raising the party’s flag as they awaited the arrival of their presidential ticket. The NDC governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, also arrived at the venue to assess the extent of the damage. A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is seen raising the party’s flag at the venue of the party’s town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos State on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV) As of the time of filing this report, the exact circumstances behind the attack and the identities of the perpetrators remained unclear, with the Lagos State Police Command yet to release an official statement. item.title: Celebrating 50 Years of Nourishment: Maltina Introduces Its New Look to Trade Partners
item.description: Maltina has unveiled its refreshed visual identity at a trade launch event in Lagos, marking 50 years of nourishing Nigerian homes and introducing a new look for the iconic malt brand while retaining the taste and nutritional qualities consumers have come to love. Held on Friday, November 6, 2026, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Ikeja, the event brought together business partners, distributors, consumers and other distinguished guests to celebrate the milestone and experience the refreshed brand through interactive activities, entertainment and product showcases. First introduced as Maltona in 1976 and renamed Maltina in 1977, the brand has maintained a strong presence in Nigerian homes for over five decades. Its journey has been defined by a commitment to nourishment, including its introduction of multivitamin enrichment in 1993 and calcium fortification in 2009. Beyond its product innovations, Maltina continues to build meaningful connections with consumers through initiatives such as Maltina Nourishment Tour, Maltina Dance All, Maltina Teacher of the Year (MTOTY), and its Christmas and Ramadan festive campaigns, creating opportunities for learning, participation and shared experiences. Speaking at the event, Sarah Agha , Marketing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., reflected on the brand’s journey and the thinking behind its refreshed identity. She highlighted Maltina’s longstanding commitment to nourishment and happiness, noting that the new look represents a more contemporary and confident expression of the brand as it prepares for its next chapter. The refreshed packaging features an enriched signature orange, gold accents and barley elements that reinforce Maltina’s malt credentials. The updated sunrays represent vitality and optimism, while the more prominent calcium coin highlights its nourishment proposition. The gold crown cork and the addition of ‘Since 1976’ further celebrate the brand’s heritage. She reassured consumers that while the brand’s visual identity has evolved, its familiar taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. She said “This is not just about refreshing our identity; it is about reaffirming our commitment to nourishment and to families across Nigeria. Our new look makes these commitments even more visible. While our identity has evolved to welcome a new chapter, our taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. It is still New Look, Same Nourishing Taste,” In his welcome address, Thibaut Boidin , Managing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., celebrated Maltina’s remarkable journey and acknowledged the consumers, partners and distributors whose continued support has contributed to the brand’s growth. He also reiterated the company’s commitment to social impact, announcing plans to support the education of children from underserved communities in the coming year. item.title: The latest FreeBSD report is here, and the AI debate is ongoing
item.description: The FreeBSD project's status team has published FreeBSD's third status report of 2026, showing plenty of ambitious work underway and a community still undecided on how to treat code from AI coding assistants. The FreeBSD Status Report Third Quarter 2026 is a substantial document, with 51 entries from five teams covering 16 projects, plus six other sections with more detailed reports. There are updates on the progress of the Sylve project, which is an attempt to bring a smooth polished GUI for managing FreeBSD virtualization hosts – something akin to Proxmox for FreeBSD. We mentioned this when we looked at the new Daemonarchy project last month. Another covers the new AppJail effort – a containerized app distribution system for FreeBSD, including for GUI apps, which aims for something broadly comparable to Snap, Flatpak and AppImage on Linux. In other words, interesting and quite radical stuff is happening in the FreeBSD space. What this particular LLM-skeptical vulture was most interested to see, though, was an update on the internal discussion about how to handle code generated by AI coding assistants in the project. We first reported on this vexed subject back in September 2025 and no final answer has yet been published. NetBSD banned AI-generated code in 2024 and although the bot-boosters say this will doom it to irrelevance, as we reported last month, the project is thriving . Also back in October, we looked at OpenBSD 8.0 , whose launch materials are full of mockery for AI users. Under the FreeBSD Core Team section , there is a subsection headed "FreeBSD Developer AI survey." The survey was created by Baptiste Daroussin, and received 140 responses. Although the percentages show that there is some resistance to AI, there are hints here as to why it’s taking so long. Some project committers are against it, yet many more are proponents. Since there are only seven bullet points, we thought we would quote them in full: Policy: 88 percent want the Project to adopt a policy, either a formal, written policy (49 percent ) or light guidance and best practices (39 percent ). Six percent said that AI should be explicitly discouraged, and three percent that the existing contribution rules are sufficient. AI-assisted code: 35 percent said it must be disclosed, 25 percent that it must be reviewed more strictly than human code, 22 percent that it should be treated like any other contribution, and 16 percent that it should be rejected outright. Safeguards: mandatory human review (78 percent ) and mandatory disclosure (69 percent ) were requested most often, followed by provenance or licensing documentation (47 percent ) and mandatory testing (39 percent ). Disclosure: 84 percent want AI use disclosed, either always (48 percent ) or when its involvement is significant (36 percent ). 79 percent want AI-assisted commits marked in the commit log, and 56 percent prefer a tag that names the tool. item.title: Microsoft admits SQL Servers might wobble after October update
item.description: Encountered some odd SQL Server connection behavior since the October update? There might be a culprit… Microsoft has admitted that a change has caused linked server queries to fail to close connections. Linked servers via OLE DB providers have been around for years and are a useful way of, for example, using additional data sources in queries. Once a provider is added, SQL Server can open a connection to grab data, and close it again when the query is complete. Or, at least, that's the theory. The problem is that after the October 13 (KB5126646) update, connections created by SQL Server linked server queries might remain open. According to Microsoft, "As additional queries are performed, connections to external databases can accumulate instead of closing as expected. "This can slow or degrade server performance after prolonged run time." You think? Administrators will likely have already noted a suspicious number of open connections to external databases on affected systems. Microsoft said the issue affects SQL Server linked server queries that use OLE DB providers to connect to external databases. It gave PostgreSQL and Oracle as examples of connections known to be affected. And the fix? "If idle connections can be identified, it is possible to manually close them to temporarily relieve server load. "It is also possible to temporarily restore system stability by restarting the SQL service." The Windows behemoth went on to state the obvious: "However, these steps can also interrupt active queries or transactions, and the problem can resurface again after sufficient operation time." Bouncing a SQL Server to deal with connection leakage is less than ideal, although it would at least be a good failover test and, let's face it, having to restart Microsoft services regularly is something many administrators will be all too familiar with. There is a mitigation available, although only through Microsoft support for business. Otherwise, an out-of-band update should be along within the next few days to deal with the problem. According to Microsoft, the technical glitch affects every version of Windows except Windows 11 26H2, stretching back to Windows 10 1809 and LTSC 2019, and Windows Server from 2025 back to 2012. Microsoft, or rather the unfortunate souls responsible for administering their server products, has not had the best time of late. The October 2026 Windows Server update left some Exchange Servers wobbling until either a Registry edit was made or a fix was applied as part of the November update. ®

item.title: How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look
item.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. Alex Unusual in her contemporary Yoruba buba and mini skirt outfit for the Loving Itohan premiere. She carried the damask into her gele, which was wrapped high into voluminous, sculptural folds. An oversized gold lip-shaped brooch secured one side, adding another detail to the headpiece. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. It’s a styling idea worth borrowing if you’re working with patterned damask and want your accessories to feel connected to the rest of your outfit. Alex Unusual pairs her damask gele with cherub-detailed sunglasses, layered gold jewellery, and custom grillz. Alex’s jewellery and accessories added even more detail. She layered a crystal floral choker with a long gold lariat necklace featuring a stirrup-style drop, then added chunky gold cuff bangles on both wrists and sculptural gold rings. item.title: European tech buyers add digital sovereignty to cyber shopping list
item.description: European tech buyers are increasingly choosing cybersecurity vendors from their own continent in a bid to reduce their reliance on American technology. Digital sovereignty isn't only prompting enterprise customers to question their clouds of choice, it is also reshaping other parts of the industry too, and the shift is marked. According to sales figures compiled by Context, distributor sales in EMEA of cybersecurity products from EU-headquartered vendors jumped 35 percent in the two years to calendar Q3 2026. Total cybersecurity sales grew up 10 percent over the same period, and sales by US-run companies went up just 8 percent. That growth is from a relatively small base, though EU vendors gained nearly three percentage points to reach 15 percent of tracked sales by value. There is still a long way to go as US-headquartered vendors accounted for 62 percent. The trend coincides with a loss of trust in the Trump administration among customers outside of America, after it cosied up to autocratic rulers while criticizing and punishing allies with tariffs and more. Context stopped short of assigning blame. It said organizations are reviewing their reliance on third-party tech in light of EU compliance regimes: the NIS2 Directive and Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). NIS2, transposed into national law in October 2024 , requires organizations in the bloc to raise their common level of security in the face of digital threats and risks to critical infrastructure. DORA, introduced in January last year, is designed to strengthen cyber security in the financial sector. "Digital sovereignty is becoming a buying decision. As customers and resellers get clearer about what it means in practice, they're asking who holds the encryption keys, who can access sensitive logs and where that data is stored," said Context veep of research Joe Turner. "We're seeing a measurable shift in the EMEA channel. EU vendors gained nearly three points of sales share in two years. An organization can keep its existing identity platform and still choose a European supplier to manage its security logs. That's the kind of decision that gives European vendors an opening." The stats indicate that EU-HQd vendors comprised 92 percent of tracked sales in security awareness training, 82 percent in vulnerability management, and 52 percent for SIEM and log management. US-headquartered companies held into 74 percent of identity and access management sales and 54 percent of cloud security sales. The Reg has asked Context for UK-specific figures to see whether British customers are also voting with their wallets for European alternatives. That certainly isn’t the case for tech purchases in the British public sector, despite Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s professed desire to buy British. Data released yesterday by the Institute for Public Policy Research showed just £1 in every £6 spent by government with the biggest technology suppliers goes to Brit businesses. item.title: Rockstar workers vote on union recognition as GTA VI launch looms
item.description: More than 1,600 Rockstar Games employees in the UK will begin voting on union recognition on Thursday, with the ballot kicking off just a week before the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The ballot, which opens on November 12 and runs until November 26, will determine whether Rockstar formally recognizes the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote. If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice. The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI. The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, although the people responsible for making it have rather more immediate concerns than sales records. "I am incredibly proud of the work we've put into making this game. I'm also proud of the union we've built here. For me, those two things are connected," said Nestor Uriate, an animation programmer and Rockstar Game Workers Union representative. "We care deeply about the games we make, and we want to make sure we can continue doing that work in an environment where we're respected, have a meaningful say over our conditions and can feel secure about our futures." The vote follows a year of bad blood between Rockstar and the IWGB. The union accused the GTA developer of union busting after it fired 31 members in October 2025, claiming they had been singled out for taking part in a private Discord group. Rockstar denied the allegations, insisting the workers were dismissed for gross misconduct rather than their union activities. The dispute subsequently reached an employment tribunal, where Rockstar unsuccessfully attempted to have blacklisting allegations struck from the case . Closing submissions are expected on November 17 and 18, meaning the legal proceedings will reach their final stages just as GTA VI prepares to hit shelves. Despite the ongoing dispute, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, recently indicated that management would respect the outcome of the recognition vote, telling Bloomberg : "We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union." The union campaign has also attracted support from elsewhere in the games industry, including SAG-AFTRA and the Communications Workers of America (CWA), which represents workers at Blizzard. item.title: Datacentres are deeply unpopular. Has Sweden made one we can all love?
item.description: It is built of wood, resembles an Ikea and its power is totally renewable. Plus, it was built with the local community in mind. Is this facility in Falun the best datacentre in the world? ‘It was pretty cool, when they were building it. It looked like a very large Ikea,” says John Wernvik, of EcoDataCenter. He is giving me a tour of their facility in Falun, Sweden, which could lay claim to being the world’s greenest datacentre – although to many, that is a contradiction in terms. One difference is immediately visible: this datacentre is made out of wood. Huge panels of cross-laminated timber arrived at the site pre-cut, and were assembled by crane according to instructions, like flatpack furniture. Aesthetically, this section of the datacentre is more like an Ikea before the fit-out, a cavernous, echoey, immaculately clean hangar. The wood is not EcoDataCenter’s only claim to sustainability; it is more than just cosmetic, says Wernvik, the company’s chief external relations and sustainability officer. “Compared with a traditional datacentre built with steel and concrete, we lower the embodied carbon of the full structure by three times.” With a complex the size of a football pitch, that is a lot of wood, but, says Wernvik, “the amount of timber one of our datacentres uses takes the Swedish forest about 10 to 15 minutes to grow back”. item.title: Five key allies of Peter Obi who parted ways with him after 2023
item.description: ‎ The recent decision by Yunusa Tanko a leading figure in the Obidient Movement, to accept an appointment as Director-General of the presidential campaign council of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate has once again drawn attention to the growing list of notable political associates who have distanced themselves from former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi. ‎ ‎Since the conclusion of the 2023 presidential election, Obi has remained one of the country’s most influential opposition politicians. ‎However, several key figures who played important roles in his campaign, political structure, or movement have either left the Labour Party, aligned with other political interests, or openly criticized his political direction. Obi is presently the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election. ‎ ‎These defections have triggered renewed debate about the cohesion of the political movement that emerged around Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign. 2027: IGP warns officers against compromise Thugs attack Pantami’s campaign rally in Gombe ‎ ‎While Obi continues to command a loyal support base across the country, the departure of several high-profile associates underscores the challenge of maintaining political unity and building a durable structure ahead of the next electoral cycle. ‎ However, his present alliance with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the leader of Kwankwasiyya Movement, is seen by many as a plus to him. ‎ ‎Below are five of such most prominent names. ‎ ‎ YUNUSA TANKO tanko yunusa ‎ ‎Perhaps the latest and most symbolic departure is that of Yunusa Tanko, who served as National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and was one of the most visible defenders of Obi after the 2023 election. ‎ ‎Tanko was a key mobiliser of Obi’s support base across the country and regularly represented the movement on national television and at political events. However, he recently accepted an appointment as Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council of SDP presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, effectively moving away from Obi’s political camp. ‎ ‎YUSUF DATTI BABA-AHMED ‎ ‎As Obi’s running mate in the 2023 election, Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed was one of the central figures of the Labour Party ticket. ‎Although he has not openly defected to another political camp in the manner of some of Obi’s former associates, reports indicate that he publicly expressed disagreements with aspects of Obi’s political direction, fueling speculation about differences within the former presidential ticket. ‎ ‎KENNETH OKONKWO ‎ ‎Actor, lawyer and politician, Kenneth Okonkwo was one of the most vocal spokespersons of the Obi campaign during the 2023 presidential race. ‎ ‎In July 2024, he announced his exit from the Labour Party and openly criticized Obi’s handling of the party’s leadership crisis.
